value.note: Live inventory of the MCP servers this origin is serving. Generated per request from the running process, so it cannot go stale. Tool names and schemas come from tools/list on each endpoint; this document carries counts only. `entrypoints` lists the root (/mcp: search over everything, ?modules= to pin a set) and the category aliases; `servers` lists the per-server endpoints. Every endpoint here is the root pinned to a module, so each also serves the six meta tools and the root's prompts and resources; the counts below are the server's own and exclude them.

entrypoints.name: AIsa
entrypoints.description: AIsa is one key for data APIs across six categories: SEO & AI visibility (DataForSEO, Semrush, Ahrefs), finance (prices, fundamentals, filings, crypto, prediction markets), social (X/Twitter, Instagram, Reddit, Pinterest, YouTube), web search & research (Tavily, Firecrawl, Exa, Perplexity), sales (Apollo, creator discovery) and agent mail (AgentMail). How to work: call search with a plain-language description of the task; it returns Router tools and sometimes a Plan. Call batch_get_schema when a result does not include its full schema. For paid operations call batch_quote with the exact calls before batch_use. A quote is an estimate, not authorization. If it reports auto_execute_eligible: true, run the successfully quoted calls unless the user set a tighter limit or asked only for a quote — the flag covers only successful quotes, so never pass a call whose quote failed; otherwise tell the user the planned calls, the quoted price and a total USD budget for the task, and after approval run calls within that budget without asking again. Every MCP request needs authorization: OAuth sign-in or an AIsa key as Authorization: Bearer; only the REST GET /search answers anonymously. search, schema lookup, list_categories, batch_quote and account are free; quotes do not execute; batch_use is billed per call to the AIsa key. `use` is deprecated compatibility; prefer batch_use. Tools listed directly in tools/list (pinned by ?modules= on the URL) can be called directly without search. To see who you are, what you can use and how much you can spend — key, account balance, the Go-to-Market wallet, usage for today / 7 days / 30 days — call account (free; use with operation_id "account" also works). It answers ok: true only when the balance was read; on ok: false follow errors[].next_step — an authentication error means the client must re-authorize AIsa. Every payment error already carries that summary and a brief balance or access error. The same metric often exists from more than one provider — domain authority from DataForSEO, Semrush and Ahrefs; backlinks from several indexes. When a decision depends on the number, cross-check two providers. Some endpoints are premium and require the Go-to-Market plan; a 402 response reports insufficient balance or account access. Everything else is pay-per-call.

usage.discover: call list_categories, or read `modules` in this document
usage.search: call search({query, known_fields?, provider_filters?, limit?, session_id?}) → Router SearchResponse with tools[], plan?, search_id and session_id
usage.prompts: one MCP prompt per category (seo, finance, social, search, sales, mail): a brief of the category, its curated operations and how to search and call; clients list them as slash commands, e.g. /mcp__aisa__seo in Claude Code
usage.details: call batch_get_schema({tools: [...], session_id?, include_arguments_schema?, include_response_schema?, include_documentation?}) for Router schemas; include_documentation: true adds the native public OpenAPI document, provenance and scoped completeness
usage.quote: call batch_quote({calls: [{call_id, tool, arguments}], session_id?, search_id?}) before paid execution
usage.use: when the quote reports auto_execute_eligible=true, or once the user's approval covers the quoted calls and cost, call batch_use with only the successfully quoted calls (unchanged), session_id and search_id — auto_execute_eligible covers only successful quotes, so drop or re-quote any call whose quote failed; use remains deprecated compatibility only
usage.pin: connect to /mcp?modules=<a>,<b> (or /<category>/mcp) to have those tools listed without searching
usage.auth: every MCP request, initialize included, needs OAuth sign-in or Authorization: Bearer <AIsa API key>; a request without one answers 401 with an OAuth challenge. Only the REST GET /search answers anonymously
usage.protocol: MCP 2026-07-28 stateless: one POST per request with headers Mcp-Method (and Mcp-Name for tools/call) and params._meta carrying protocolVersion and clientCapabilities; no initialize
usage.account: call account (or use({operation_id: 'account'}) on older clients) → ok, key, balances, Go-to-Market wallet, usage today/7d/30d; free. ok: false carries errors[].next_step. Attached automatically to every payment error
usage.contract: search, batch_get_schema, batch_quote and batch_use use the matching Tool Router REST contracts; get_details is an unlisted alias of batch_get_schema, kept for existing clients

previous_value.note: Live inventory of the MCP servers this origin is serving. Generated per request from the running process, so it cannot go stale. Tool names and schemas come from tools/list on each endpoint; this document carries counts only. `entrypoints` lists the root (/mcp: search over everything, ?modules= to pin a set) and the category aliases; `servers` lists the per-server endpoints. Every endpoint here is the root pinned to a module, so each also serves the six meta tools and the root's prompts and resources; the counts below are the server's own and exclude them.

entrypoints.name: AIsa
entrypoints.description: AIsa is one key for data APIs across six categories: SEO & AI visibility (DataForSEO, Semrush, Ahrefs), finance (prices, fundamentals, filings, crypto, prediction markets), social (X/Twitter, Instagram, Reddit, Pinterest, YouTube), web search & research (Tavily, Firecrawl, Exa, Perplexity), sales (Apollo, creator discovery) and agent mail (AgentMail). How to work: call search with a plain-language description of the task; it returns Router tools and sometimes a Plan. Call batch_get_schema when a result does not include its full schema. For paid operations call batch_quote with the exact calls before batch_use. A quote is an estimate, not authorization. If it reports auto_execute_eligible: true, run the successfully quoted calls unless the user set a tighter limit or asked only for a quote — the flag covers only successful quotes, so never pass a call whose quote failed; otherwise tell the user the planned calls, the quoted price and a total USD budget for the task, and after approval run calls within that budget without asking again. Every MCP request needs authorization: OAuth sign-in or an AIsa key as Authorization: Bearer; only the REST GET /search answers anonymously. search, schema lookup, list_categories, batch_quote and account are free; quotes do not execute; batch_use is billed per call to the AIsa key. `use` is deprecated compatibility; prefer batch_use. Tools listed directly in tools/list (pinned by ?modules= on the URL) can be called directly without search. To see who you are, what you can use and how much you can spend — key, account balance, the Go-to-Market wallet, usage for today / 7 days / 30 days — call account (free; use with operation_id "account" also works). It answers ok: true only when the balance was read; on ok: false follow errors[].next_step — an authentication error means the client must re-authorize AIsa. Every payment error already carries that summary and a brief balance or access error. The same metric often exists from more than one provider — domain authority from DataForSEO, Semrush and Ahrefs; backlinks from several indexes. When a decision depends on the number, cross-check two providers. Some endpoints are premium and require the Go-to-Market plan; a 402 response reports insufficient balance or account access. Everything else is pay-per-call.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.title: Browse the AIsa catalogue
tools.description: The AIsa catalogue at a glance: categories, the servers in each, tool counts, and the dedicated endpoint to connect if you only need one category. Free. (AIsa-only: tool-router has no equivalent.) Use `mcp.aisa.one/mcp?modules=<category>` (or `mcp.aisa.one/<category>/mcp`) to have that category's tools listed directly instead of via search.

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search AIsa tools and agent-ready plans
tools.description: Discover AIsa tools and Plans for external data or actions. Skip tasks that only need supplied content or general knowledge. For multi-step tasks, search the full goal before decomposing it. Use English; put identifiers in known_fields. If has_full_schema=false, call batch_get_schema. Next call batch_quote, not batch_use. Do not search for standalone rewriting, translation, summarization, formatting, or calculations on supplied content. For one capability, use an atomic query. Select a matching capability, date window, and metric. A Plan may cover only part of the task; assess its purpose and follow next_steps_guidance.

tools.name: batch_get_schema
tools.title: Get AIsa tool schemas in one batch
tools.description: Retrieve schemas for 1 to 20 exact tool names from search. Build arguments from successful schemas, then call batch_quote. Do not call batch_use yet. Use tool names exactly as search returns them, without a client prefix such as mcp__aisa__. Reuse the session_id returned by Search in all subsequent tool calls for this task. If omitted, a new session is created.

tools.name: batch_quote
tools.title: Quote published AIsa tools without executing them
tools.description: Obtain AIsaServices cost quotes for 1 to 20 published tools without executing them. Same input as batch_use: exact tool names and schema-valid arguments. Never falls back to execution. The response reports auto_execute_eligible and auto_execute_threshold_micros_usd. auto_execute_eligible waives only the extra cost-confirmation step and does not override a user prohibition on execution, a narrower scope, or a tighter budget limit. Quotes are price observations, not authorization grants. Use tool names exactly as search returns them, without a client prefix such as mcp__aisa__. Reuse the session_id returned by Search in all subsequent tool calls for this task. If omitted, a new session is created.

tools.name: batch_use
tools.title: Execute published AIsa tools
tools.description: Billable API calls can incur substantial charges. Never call before a successful batch_quote for the same tools and arguments. Execute only when that quote response reports auto_execute_eligible=true for these calls, or when explicit user authorization covers that cost and risk. auto_execute_eligible waives only the extra cost-confirmation step; it does not override a user prohibition on execution, a narrower scope, or a tighter budget limit. Re-quote if tools, arguments, or scope change. Execute 1 to 20 independent published-tool calls; never silently retry. A missing or failed quote is not free. Use tool names exactly as search returns them, without a client prefix such as mcp__aisa__. Reuse the session_id returned by Search in all subsequent tool calls for this task. If omitted, a new session is created.

tools.name: account
tools.title: Show account and usage
tools.description: Who am I, what can I use, how much can I spend: the key, the account balance, the Go-to-Market wallet when one is active, and usage for today, 7 days and 30 days. Free; needs the Authorization header. Call it to verify a new connection or to explain a 402. `ok` is true only when the balance was read; otherwise each entry of `errors` says what to do in `next_step`.

usage.discover: call list_categories, or read `modules` in this document
usage.search: call search({query, known_fields?, provider_filters?, limit?, session_id?}) → Router SearchResponse with tools[], plan?, search_id and session_id
usage.prompts: one MCP prompt per category (seo, finance, social, search, sales, mail): a brief of the category, its curated operations and how to search and call; clients list them as slash commands, e.g. /mcp__aisa__seo in Claude Code
usage.details: call batch_get_schema({tools: [...], session_id?, include_arguments_schema?, include_response_schema?, include_documentation?}) for Router schemas; include_documentation: true adds the native public OpenAPI document, provenance and scoped completeness
usage.quote: call batch_quote({calls: [{call_id, tool, arguments}], session_id?, search_id?}) before paid execution
usage.use: when the quote reports auto_execute_eligible=true, or once the user's approval covers the quoted calls and cost, call batch_use with only the successfully quoted calls (unchanged), session_id and search_id — auto_execute_eligible covers only successful quotes, so drop or re-quote any call whose quote failed; use remains deprecated compatibility only
usage.pin: connect to /mcp?modules=<a>,<b> (or /<category>/mcp) to have those tools listed without searching
usage.auth: every MCP request, initialize included, needs OAuth sign-in or Authorization: Bearer <AIsa API key>; a request without one answers 401 with an OAuth challenge. Only the REST GET /search answers anonymously
usage.protocol: MCP 2026-07-28 stateless: one POST per request with headers Mcp-Method (and Mcp-Name for tools/call) and params._meta carrying protocolVersion and clientCapabilities; no initialize
usage.account: call account (or use({operation_id: 'account'}) on older clients) → ok, key, balances, Go-to-Market wallet, usage today/7d/30d; free. ok: false carries errors[].next_step. Attached automatically to every payment error
usage.contract: search, batch_get_schema, batch_quote and batch_use use the matching Tool Router REST contracts; get_details is an unlisted alias of batch_get_schema, kept for existing clients

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://aisa.one/docs/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

> ## Agent Instructions
> - Base URLs: models `https://api.aisa.one/v1` (Gemini GenerateContent: `https://api.aisa.one/v1beta`); data APIs `https://api.aisa.one/apis/v1`. The `servers` of each operation in https://aisa.one/openapi.yaml is authoritative.
> - Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY`. Never print, log, or commit the key.
> - MCP (preferred for agents): `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp`, signed in with OAuth, so there is no key to paste.
> - Agent Skill: `npx skills add AIsa-team/agent-skills --skill aisa`. Fallback with the AIsa CLI: `aisa skills install aisa`.
> - Spending: docs, https://aisa.one/models, https://aisa.one/api, `/v1/models`, and MCP `search`, `list_categories`, `get_details`, `batch_quote`, and the `account` operation are free. Quote the exact calls before running them (MCP `batch_quote`, CLI `aisa quote --json`). If the quote reports `auto_execute_eligible: true`, run it unless the user set a tighter limit or asked only for a quote. Otherwise, tell the user in one message the planned calls, the quoted price, and a total USD budget for the task, then wait for approval. Direct HTTP calls follow the stricter rule at https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/cli.md#direct-http-fallback. Do not make paid calls to test availability. Full rule: https://aisa.one/llms.txt

# Connect your agent to AIsa

> Add the AIsa MCP server to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or other agents, sign in with browser OAuth, and start using tools. Use the CLI only when MCP cannot run.

**AI agent reading this?** Go to [Agent instructions](#agent-instructions) and run the setup yourself.

AIsa provides a remote MCP server at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp`. Authentication uses browser OAuth, so there is no API key to copy.

**1. Add the server**

```bash Claude Code theme={null}
claude mcp add --transport http -s user aisa https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp
```

```bash Codex theme={null}
codex mcp add aisa --url https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp
```


# Authentication

> How AIsa authenticates requests: API keys as Bearer tokens for HTTP and SDKs, and OAuth sign-in for MCP and the CLI. Key limits, storage, rotation, and revocation.

AIsa accepts two kinds of credentials. Both draw on the same account balance.

| Credential | Used by | How you get it |
| - | - | - |
| **OAuth sign-in** | MCP clients (`https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp`), the AIsa CLI | Approve once in the browser; the client stores and refreshes the token |
| **API key** | HTTP requests, SDKs, CI, servers | Create it in [Console → API Keys](https://console.aisa.one/api-keys) |

Agents should prefer OAuth: nobody copies a secret, and the user can sign out without rotating keys. Use an API key when code runs without a person present.

## OAuth for MCP and the CLI

You do not create anything in advance.

* **MCP.** Add `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` to your client. On first use the server answers `401` with OAuth metadata (RFC 9728), the client opens a browser, and you click **Allow**. The client keeps the token; agents must not read or reuse it. Steps per client: [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md).
* **CLI.** `aisa login` runs the same browser flow and stores an auto-refreshing session in `~/.aisa/tokens.json`. Check it with `aisa balance`. See [Use the CLI](https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/cli.md).

An MCP client can also send an API key instead (`Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY`) when OAuth is not possible, for example in CI. For the CLI, setting `AISA_API_KEY` overrides the stored session.

Some account-wide views need OAuth. For example, `GET /v1/usage` with `scope=account` requires an OAuth session; an API key can only read its own usage.

## API keys

Send the key as a Bearer token on every request:

```bash theme={null}
curl https://api.aisa.one/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"qwen3.7-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Before your first top-up, the account runs on signup credit and only models marked `"recharge_required": false` in `GET /v1/models` can be called. Other models return `402` with `error.code = "recharge_required"` until you add credit.

The same key works for models (`https://api.aisa.one/v1`), data APIs (`https://api.aisa.one/apis/v1`), and MCP. The Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` route also accepts it as `x-api-key`, which is what the Anthropic SDK sends. See [OpenAI / Anthropic SDK](https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/sdk-compatibility.md).

### Key settings

When you create or edit a key in [API Keys](https://console.aisa.one/api-keys) you can set:

* **Name** - label the key by app or environment, such as `prod-web` or `ci`.
* **Spending limit** - the most this key may spend, in USD, or **Unlimited**. The key can spend up to the lower of its remaining limit and your account balance. When the limit runs out the key's status becomes *exhausted* and requests return `402 insufficient_api_key_balance`.
* **Allowed IPs** - restrict the key to specific IP addresses or CIDR ranges.
* **Status** - disable a key temporarily without deleting it.

A practical pattern is one key per service or environment - a development key with a small limit, a production key with a larger one - so revoking one never interrupts the others.

### Rotate and revoke

To rotate: create a new key, deploy it everywhere, confirm in [Usage & Logs](https://console.aisa.one/logs) that the old key has stopped receiving traffic, then revoke the old key. Rotate on a schedule and immediately after anyone with access leaves.

If a key leaks, **revoke it first** and investigate afterwards. Requests with a disabled, expired, or invalid key return `401` (`api_key_disabled`, `expired_api_key`, `invalid_api_key`). See [Errors](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/errors.md).

## Storing keys

> [!WARNING]
>
> Your API key has direct access to spend your account balance. Never commit it to git repositories, share it in chat, or include it in client-side code.

> [accordion] Local development
>
> Keep the key in a `.env` file loaded by `python-dotenv` or `dotenv`, and add `.env` to `.gitignore`.
>
> ```bash theme={null}
> # .env
> AISA_API_KEY=sk-...
> ```

> [accordion] CI/CD
>
> Store the key as a CI secret and expose it as an environment variable. Give CI its own key with a low spending limit.
>
> ```yaml theme={null}
> # GitHub Actions
> env:
>   AISA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.AISA_API_KEY }}
> ```

> [accordion] Servers and cloud
>
> Use your platform's secret manager (AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, or the encrypted environment variables of Fly, Render, or Railway). Rotating the secret and restarting picks up the new key.

> [accordion] Client-side apps
>
> Never put a key in code a user can inspect. Call AIsa from a backend you control that authenticates your users, applies per-user limits, and forwards requests with the server-held key.

## Related

> [card] [Billing & Credits](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/pricing.md)
>
> How spend is metered, quoted, and capped.

> [card] [Security & Privacy](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/security.md)
>
> Data handling, retention, and transport security.

## Settled call cost

For Integration API responses that report a settled customer debit,
`X-AISA-Customer-Cost-Micros-USD` contains a nonnegative decimal integer in
micro-USD: `1000000` means `$1.00`. A returned `0` means the reported debit is
zero. A missing or malformed header means the response did not supply a usable
settled amount; **missing does not mean free**. Do not infer a debit solely from
HTTP success or failure, a price tier, or a catalog estimate.

The gateway exposes this customer-cost header through
`Access-Control-Expose-Headers` for browser callers. Its accepted integer range
is `0` through `9223372036854775807`; use an integer/decimal representation, not a
floating-point conversion, when reconciling money. JavaScript callers should use
`BigInt` for micro-USD or preserve the decimal string.

| Response path | Cost-header policy |
| - | - |
| Metered V2 settlement | Can return both `X-AISA-Customer-Cost-Micros-USD` and `X-AISA-Provider-Cost-Micros-USD`. Provider cost is separate accounting evidence, not the customer's debit; fallback evidence may be an estimate. |
| Fixed/default settlement | Reports the settled customer debit, including zero; does not expose a new Provider-cost micro-USD header and removes an upstream-supplied one. |
| Quote, pre-settlement rejection, transport failure, or special no-charge path | A settled header may be absent. Follow the endpoint's quote or error contract; absence does not establish zero cost. |

Provider-cost headers are not part of the common browser CORS exposed-header
list. They are endpoint/strategy-specific; this page does not promise their
presence or expand their exposure. In particular, web-search-specific cost
headers are not a universal Integration API contract.

A cost quote is an estimate or bound returned before execution, not proof of a
settled charge. The `X-AISA-Max-Price-USD` request header is a spending cap, not a
reported debit. MCP result fields depend on the deployed version. When
`customer_cost_micros_usd` and `cost_usd_exact` are provided, use them to preserve
the reported amount; `cost_usd` is a numeric display and can round very large
values. Do not assume every MCP deployment supplies the exact fields. Unknown
cost remains absent, including on an error. A quoted
`estimated_cost_micros_usd` must not be substituted for a settled amount.

The following Python example accepts a case-insensitive HTTP headers mapping
(such as `requests.Response.headers`) and preserves exact decimal output:

```python theme={null}
def settled_customer_cost(headers):
    raw = headers.get("X-AISA-Customer-Cost-Micros-USD")
    if raw is None:
        return None
    value = str(raw).strip()
    if not value.isascii() or not value.isdecimal():
        return None
    micros = int(value)
    if micros > 9223372036854775807:
        return None
    return {
        "customer_cost_micros_usd": micros,
        "cost_usd_exact": f"{micros // 1000000}.{micros % 1000000:06d}",
    }
```

See [Error Codes](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/errors.md) for retained response formats and safe
retry handling.

# Gemini Generate Content

> Generate content using a Gemini-compatible AIsa model

## Request contract

* **Method and path:** POST /models/\{model}:generateContent
* **Request URL template:** `https://api.aisa.one/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`
* **model:** path; required

[Complete OpenAPI definition](https://aisa.one/docs/openapi/gemini-openapi.json)

Effective request and pricing declaration (including authentication and referenced schemas):

```json theme={null}
{
  "operationId": "generateContent",
  "method": "POST",
  "path": "/models/{model}:generateContent",
  "servers": [
    {
      "description": "Gemini-compatible API base URL",
      "url": "https://api.aisa.one/v1beta"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": [
    {
      "description": "The AIsa model ID to use, for example: gemini-3.5-flash.",
      "in": "path",
      "name": "model",
      "required": true,
      "schema": {
        "example": "gemini-3.5-flash",
        "type": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "security": [
    {
      "BearerAuth": []
    }
  ],
  "requestBody": {
    "content": {
      "application/json": {
        "schema": {
          "$ref": "#/components/schemas/GenerateContentRequest"
        }
      }
    },
    "required": true
  },
  "components": {
    "schemas": {
      "GenerateContentRequest": {
        "properties": {
          "cachedContent": {
            "description": "Optional cached content ID",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "contents": {
            "description": "Content of the conversation, required",
            "items": {
              "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Content"
            },
            "type": "array"
          },
          "generationConfig": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/GenerationConfig"
          },
          "safetySettings": {
            "items": {
              "$ref": "#/components/schemas/SafetySetting"
            },
            "type": "array"
          },
          "systemInstruction": {
            "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Content"
          },
          "toolConfig": {
            "description": "Optional tool configuration",
            "type": "object"
          },
          "tools": {
            "description": "Optional tools the model can use",
            "items": {
              "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Tool"
            },
            "type": "array"
          }
        },
        "required": [
          "contents"
        ],
        "type": "object"
      },
      "Content": {
        "additionalProperties": true,
        "properties": {
          "parts": {
            "items": {
              "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Part"
            },
            "type": "array"
          },
          "role": {
            "enum": [

              "system",
              "assistant"

            "type": "string"

        "type": "object"

        "additionalProperties": true,
        "properties": {
          "inline_data": {
            "description": "Inline binary data for multimodal content.",
            "type": "object"

          "text": {
            "description": "Generated or input text content.",
            "type": "string"
          },
          "thoughtSignature": {
            "description": "Provider-generated thought signature metadata.",
            "type": "string"
          }
        },
        "type": "object"
      },
      "GenerationConfig": {
        "type": "object"
      },
      "SafetySetting": {
        "type": "object"
      },
      "Tool": {
        "type": "object"
      }
    },
    "securitySchemes": {
      "BearerAuth": {
        "bearerFormat": "API Key",
```

````yaml openapi/gemini-openapi.json POST /models/{model}:generateContent
info:

          description: Successful content generation
        default:
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse'
          description: Error response
      security:

components:

      properties:

          description: Optional cached content ID

          description: Content of the conversation, required
          items:

          type: array
        generationConfig:

        safetySettings:
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/SafetySetting'
          type: array

          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Content'
        toolConfig:
          description: Optional tool configuration
          type: object
        tools:
          description: Optional tools the model can use
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Tool'
          type: array
      required:
        - contents
      type: object
    GenerateContentResponse:
      additionalProperties: true
      properties:
        candidates:
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Candidate'
          type: array
        modelVersion:
          type: string
        responseId:
          type: string
        usageMetadata:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/UsageMetadata'
      type: object
    ErrorResponse:
      properties:
        error:
          properties:
            code:
              type: integer
            message:
              type: string
            status:
              type: string
          type: object
      type: object
    Content:
      additionalProperties: true
      properties:
        parts:
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Part'
          type: array
        role:
          enum:
            - user
            - model
            - system
            - assistant
          type: string
      type: object
    GenerationConfig:
      type: object
    SafetySetting:
      type: object
    Tool:
      type: object
    Candidate:
      additionalProperties: true
      properties:
        content:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Content'
        finishReason:
          type: string
        index:
          type: integer
        safetyRatings:
          items:
            type: object
          type: array
      type: object
    UsageMetadata:
      additionalProperties: true
      properties:
        candidatesTokenCount:
          type: integer
        promptTokenCount:
          type: integer
        totalTokenCount:
          type: integer
      type: object
    Part:
      additionalProperties: true
      properties:
        inline_data:
          description: Inline binary data for multimodal content.
          type: object
        text:
          description: Generated or input text content.
          type: string
        thoughtSignature:
          description: Provider-generated thought signature metadata.
          type: string
      type: object
  securitySchemes:
    BearerAuth:
      bearerFormat: API Key
      scheme: bearer
      type: http
````

# OpenAI-Compatible Image Generations

> Generate images with Seedream, Wan, gpt-image-2, and GPT Image 2.5 via the standard POST /v1/images/generations endpoint. OpenAI-compatible request shape; Seedream routes require a minimum image size of 3,686,400 pixels (e.g., 1920×1920).

The standard OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/images/generations` endpoint. As of September 30, 2026 it serves `seedream-5-0-260128`, `wan2.7-image`, `wan2.7-image-pro`, `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`. No image model is served on `POST /v1/chat/completions` — image generation goes through this endpoint (and `POST /v1/images/edits` where noted).

## Routing at a glance

| Model | Endpoint |
| - | - |
| `seedream-5-0-260128` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)* |
| `wan2.7-image` / `wan2.7-image-pro` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `gpt-image-2` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `gpt-image-2.5-flare` / `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| Gemini-compatible models | [`POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/chat/post_models-model-generatecontent) |

## Supported models

| Model | Billed by | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `seedream-5-0-260128` | Per request | Min image size **3,686,400 pixels** (e.g., 1920×1920) |
| `wan2.7-image` | Per request | Also accepts `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `wan2.7-image-pro` | Per request | Higher-quality Wan route |
| `gpt-image-2` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache write | See [AI Model Pricing](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/pricing.md#models) |
| `gpt-image-2.5-flare` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read | GPT Image 2.5 route |
| `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read | GPT Image 2.5 route |

Current prices are on [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models).

## Size constraint ⚠️ (Seedream routes)

Seedream's upstream enforces a minimum of **3,686,400 pixels**. Requests below that are rejected with:

```
400 InvalidParameter: image size must be at least 3686400 pixels
```

| Size | Pixels | Accepted? |
| - | - | - |
| `1024x1024` | 1,048,576 | ❌ |
| `1536x1536` | 2,359,296 | ❌ |
| `1920x1920` | 3,686,400 | ✅ (exact threshold) |
| `2048x2048` | 4,194,304 | ✅ |
| `2304x1600` | 3,686,400 | ✅ |
| `2560x1920` | 4,915,200 | ✅ |

Any aspect ratio works as long as `width × height ≥ 3,686,400`.

## Request

```bash curl theme={null}
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.aisa.one/v1/images/generations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "seedream-5-0-260128",
    "prompt": "A cute red panda, ultra-detailed, cinematic lighting",
    "n": 1,
    "size": "2048x2048"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.aisa.one/v1", api_key="sk-aisa-...")

resp = client.images.generate(
    model="seedream-5-0-260128",
    prompt="A cute red panda, ultra-detailed, cinematic lighting",
    n=1,
    size="2048x2048",
)

for item in resp.data:
    print(item.url)
```

```typescript TypeScript theme={null}
import OpenAI from "openai";

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://api.aisa.one/v1",
  apiKey: process.env.AISA_API_KEY,
});

const resp = await client.images.generate({
  model: "seedream-5-0-260128",
  prompt: "A cute red panda, ultra-detailed, cinematic lighting",
  n: 1,
  size: "2048x2048",
});

for (const item of resp.data) {
  console.log(item.url);
}
```

### Request fields

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| - | - | - | - |
| `model` | string | yes | One of `seedream-5-0-260128`, `wan2.7-image`, `wan2.7-image-pro`, `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` |
| `prompt` | string | yes | Text description of the image to generate |
| `n` | integer | no | Number of images. A per-request model charges one request price whatever `n` is; a token-priced model charges the tokens it reports |
| `size` | string | no | `WIDTHxHEIGHT`. Seedream routes must satisfy `width × height ≥ 3,686,400`; `wan2.7-image` and `gpt-image-2` accept smaller sizes (`1024x1024` verified working) |

## Response

```json theme={null}
{
  "model": "seedream-5-0-260128",
  "created": 1776495432,
  "data": [
    {
      "url": "https://cdn.aisa.one/images/seedream/...",
      "size": "2048x2048"
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "generated_images": 1,
    "output_tokens": 16384,
    "total_tokens": 16384
  }
}
```

**AIsa's response adds a few extensions** over the vanilla OpenAI schema:

* `model` echoed at the root
* `data[].size` — actual dimensions of each returned image
* `usage` — as the model reports it, for example `generated_images`, `output_tokens` and `total_tokens`. Token-priced models are charged from the token counts; per-request models are charged once per request

> [!WARNING]
>
> URLs in `data[].url` are **short-lived**. Download and persist the image to your own storage before it expires.

## Common 4xx causes

* `400 InvalidParameter — image size must be at least 3686400 pixels` — `size` was too small. Use `1920x1920` or larger.
* `400 model_route_not_supported` — the model doesn't serve this endpoint (e.g., a text model like `gpt-4.1-mini`). The error body's `supported_routes` lists the routes it does serve.
* `404 model not found` — the model ID doesn't exist on the gateway (e.g., the retired `seedream-4-5-251128`). Check the [model catalog](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/models.md).
* `400 invalid_request` — malformed `size` string (e.g., `1024` instead of `1024x1024`).

See [Error Codes](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/errors.md) and [Rate Limits](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/rate-limits.md) for more.

> Generate images with Seedream, Wan, gpt-image-2, and GPT Image 2.5 via the standard POST /v1/images/generations endpoint. OpenAI-compatible request shape; Seedream routes require a minimum image size of 3,686,400 pixels (e.g., 1920×1920).

The standard OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/images/generations` endpoint. As of September 30, 2026 it serves `seedream-5-0-260128`, `wan2.7-image`, `wan2.7-image-pro`, `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`. No image model is served on `POST /v1/chat/completions` — image generation goes through this endpoint (and `POST /v1/images/edits` where noted).

## Routing at a glance

| Model | Endpoint |
| - | - |
| `seedream-5-0-260128` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)* |
| `wan2.7-image` / `wan2.7-image-pro` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `gpt-image-2` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `gpt-image-2.5-flare` / `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| Gemini-compatible models | [`POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/chat/post_models-model-generatecontent) |

## Supported models

| Model | Billed by | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `seedream-5-0-260128` | Per request | Min image size **3,686,400 pixels** (e.g., 1920×1920) |
| `wan2.7-image` | Per request | Also accepts `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `wan2.7-image-pro` | Per request | Higher-quality Wan route |
| `gpt-image-2` | Per request or per image; token pricing also applies on some routes | See [AI Model Pricing](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/pricing.md#models) |
| `gpt-image-2.5-flare` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read | GPT Image 2.5 route |

## Size constraint ⚠️ (Seedream routes)

Seedream's upstream enforces a minimum of **3,686,400 pixels**. Requests below that are rejected with:

```
400 InvalidParameter: image size must be at least 3686400 pixels
```

| Size | Pixels | Accepted? |
| - | - | - |
| `1024x1024` | 1,048,576 | ❌ |
| `1536x1536` | 2,359,296 | ❌ |
| `1920x1920` | 3,686,400 | ✅ (exact threshold) |
| `2048x2048` | 4,194,304 | ✅ |
| `2304x1600` | 3,686,400 | ✅ |
| `2560x1920` | 4,915,200 | ✅ |

Any aspect ratio works as long as `width × height ≥ 3,686,400`.

## Response

```json theme={null}
{
  "model": "seedream-5-0-260128",
  "created": 1776495432,
  "data": [

      "size": "2048x2048"
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "generated_images": 1,
    "output_tokens": 16384,
    "total_tokens": 16384
  }

```

**AIsa's response adds a few extensions** over the vanilla OpenAI schema:

* `model` echoed at the root
* `data[].size` — actual dimensions of each returned image
* `usage` — includes `generated_images` (drives billing), plus `output_tokens` / `total_tokens` for token accounting

> [!WARNING]
>
> URLs in `data[].url` are **short-lived**. Download and persist the image to your own storage before it expires.

## Common 4xx causes

* `400 InvalidParameter — image size must be at least 3686400 pixels` — `size` was too small. Use `1920x1920` or larger.

* `404 model not found` — the model ID doesn't exist on the gateway (e.g., the retired `seedream-4-5-251128`). Check the [model catalog](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/models.md).
* `400 invalid_request` — malformed `size` string (e.g., `1024` instead of `1024x1024`).

# OpenAI-Compatible Image Generations

> Generate images with Seedream, Wan, gpt-image-2, and GPT Image 2.5 via the standard POST /v1/images/generations endpoint. OpenAI-compatible request shape; Seedream routes require a minimum image size of 3,686,400 pixels (e.g., 1920×1920).

The standard OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/images/generations` endpoint. As of September 30, 2026 it serves `seedream-5-0-260128`, `wan2.7-image`, `wan2.7-image-pro`, `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`. No image model is served on `POST /v1/chat/completions` — image generation goes through this endpoint (and `POST /v1/images/edits` where noted).

## Routing at a glance

| Model | Endpoint |
| - | - |
| `seedream-5-0-260128` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)* |
| `wan2.7-image` / `wan2.7-image-pro` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `gpt-image-2` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `gpt-image-2.5-flare` / `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| Gemini-compatible models | [`POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/chat/post_models-model-generatecontent) |

## Supported models

| Model | Billed by | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `seedream-5-0-260128` | Per request | Min image size **3,686,400 pixels** (e.g., 1920×1920) |
| `wan2.7-image` | Per request | Also accepts `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `wan2.7-image-pro` | Per request | Higher-quality Wan route |
| `gpt-image-2` | Per request or per image; token pricing also applies on some routes | See [AI Model Pricing](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/pricing.md#models) |
| `gpt-image-2.5-flare` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read | GPT Image 2.5 route |
| `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read | GPT Image 2.5 route |

Current prices are on [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models).

## Size constraint ⚠️ (Seedream routes)

Seedream's upstream enforces a minimum of **3,686,400 pixels**. Requests below that are rejected with:

```
400 InvalidParameter: image size must be at least 3686400 pixels
```

| Size | Pixels | Accepted? |
| - | - | - |
| `1024x1024` | 1,048,576 | ❌ |
| `1536x1536` | 2,359,296 | ❌ |
| `1920x1920` | 3,686,400 | ✅ (exact threshold) |
| `2048x2048` | 4,194,304 | ✅ |
| `2304x1600` | 3,686,400 | ✅ |
| `2560x1920` | 4,915,200 | ✅ |

Any aspect ratio works as long as `width × height ≥ 3,686,400`.

## Request

```bash curl theme={null}
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.aisa.one/v1/images/generations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "seedream-5-0-260128",
    "prompt": "A cute red panda, ultra-detailed, cinematic lighting",
    "n": 1,
    "size": "2048x2048"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.aisa.one/v1", api_key="sk-aisa-...")

resp = client.images.generate(
    model="seedream-5-0-260128",
    prompt="A cute red panda, ultra-detailed, cinematic lighting",
    n=1,
    size="2048x2048",
)

for item in resp.data:
    print(item.url)
```

### Request fields

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| - | - | - | - |
| `model` | string | yes | One of `seedream-5-0-260128`, `wan2.7-image`, `wan2.7-image-pro`, `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` |
| `prompt` | string | yes | Text description of the image to generate |
| `n` | integer | no | Number of images. Each is billed separately at the model's per-request rate |
| `size` | string | no | `WIDTHxHEIGHT`. Seedream routes must satisfy `width × height ≥ 3,686,400`; `wan2.7-image` and `gpt-image-2` accept smaller sizes (`1024x1024` verified working) |

## Response

```json theme={null}
{
  "model": "seedream-5-0-260128",
  "created": 1776495432,
  "data": [
    {
      "url": "https://cdn.aisa.one/images/seedream/...",
      "size": "2048x2048"
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "generated_images": 1,
    "output_tokens": 16384,
    "total_tokens": 16384
  }
}
```

**AIsa's response adds a few extensions** over the vanilla OpenAI schema:

* `model` echoed at the root
* `data[].size` — actual dimensions of each returned image
* `usage` — includes `generated_images` (drives billing), plus `output_tokens` / `total_tokens` for token accounting

> [!WARNING]
>
> URLs in `data[].url` are **short-lived**. Download and persist the image to your own storage before it expires.

## Common 4xx causes

* `400 InvalidParameter — image size must be at least 3686400 pixels` — `size` was too small. Use `1920x1920` or larger.
* `400 model_route_not_supported` — the model doesn't serve this endpoint (e.g., a text model like `gpt-4.1-mini`). The error body's `supported_routes` lists the routes it does serve.
* `404 model not found` — the model ID doesn't exist on the gateway (e.g., the retired `seedream-4-5-251128`). Check the [model catalog](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/models.md).
* `400 invalid_request` — malformed `size` string (e.g., `1024` instead of `1024x1024`).

See [Error Codes](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/errors.md) and [Rate Limits](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/rate-limits.md) for more.

# Coin Data by ID

> Everything CoinGecko holds on one coin: profile, links, categories, contract addresses and full market data.

Everything CoinGecko holds on one coin, selected by `id`: `description`, `links`, `image`, `categories`, `platforms` and `detail_platforms` (contract addresses per chain), `market_cap_rank`, and a `market_data` block carrying `current_price`, `market_cap`, `total_volume`, `fully_diluted_valuation`, `ath` and `atl` with dates and change percentages. The heavy sections are opt-in via `market_data`, `community_data`, `developer_data`, `tickers`, `sparkline` and `localization` — leave them off unless needed, the full payload is large. Use it for a coin profile. For a price table across many coins use [`get_coingecko_coins_markets`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-markets); to look the same coin up by contract address use [`get_coingecko_token_data`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-contract-contract-address).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

> ## Agent Instructions
> - Base URLs: models `https://api.aisa.one/v1` (Gemini GenerateContent: `https://api.aisa.one/v1beta`); data APIs `https://api.aisa.one/apis/v1`. The `servers` of each operation in https://aisa.one/openapi.yaml is authoritative.
> - Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY`. Never print, log, or commit the key.
> - MCP (preferred for agents): `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp`, signed in with OAuth, so there is no key to paste.
> - Agent Skill: `npx skills add AIsa-team/agent-skills --skill aisa`. Fallback with the AIsa CLI: `aisa skills install aisa`.
> - Spending: docs, https://aisa.one/models, https://aisa.one/api, `/v1/models`, and MCP `search`, `list_categories`, `get_details`, `batch_quote`, and the `account` operation are free. Quote the exact calls before running them (MCP `batch_quote`, CLI `aisa quote --json`). If the quote reports `auto_execute_eligible: true`, run it unless the user set a tighter limit or asked only for a quote. Otherwise, tell the user in one message the planned calls, the quoted price, and a total USD budget for the task, then wait for approval. Direct HTTP calls follow the stricter rule at https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/cli.md#direct-http-fallback. Do not make paid calls to test availability. Full rule: https://aisa.one/llms.txt

# Coin Data by Token Address

> A full coin profile looked up by contract address instead of CoinGecko id.

A full coin profile looked up by contract address instead of CoinGecko id. `id` is the asset platform and `contract_address` the token; both are required and there are no other parameters. Returns the same shape as [`get_coingecko_coins_id`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id) — `description`, `links`, `image`, `categories`, `platforms`, `detail_platforms`, `market_cap_rank`, a `market_data` block and an embedded `tickers` array — plus `contract_address` itself. Use it to identify an unknown token from an address. If only the current price is needed, [`get_coingecko_simple_token_price_id`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-simple-token-price-id) is far lighter.

> [!NOTE]
>

# Coin Data by Token Address

> A full coin profile looked up by contract address instead of CoinGecko id.

A full coin profile looked up by contract address instead of CoinGecko id. `id` is the asset platform and `contract_address` the token; both are required and there are no other parameters. Returns the same shape as [`get_coingecko_coins_id`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id) — `description`, `links`, `image`, `categories`, `platforms`, `detail_platforms`, `market_cap_rank`, a `market_data` block and an embedded `tickers` array — plus `contract_address` itself. Use it to identify an unknown token from an address. If only the current price is needed, [`get_coingecko_simple_token_price_id`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-simple-token-price-id) is far lighter.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

[Set this endpoint up in your agent →](https://aisa.one/mcp?from=/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-contract-contract-address)

# Coin Historical Chart Data by Token Address

> Price, market cap and volume history for a token identified by its contract address.

Historical series for a token identified by contract address, over a trailing window set by `days`. `id` is the asset platform, `contract_address` the token. Returns `prices`, `market_caps` and `total_volumes` as timestamp-and-value pairs, with timestamps in milliseconds — the same shape as [`get_coingecko_coins_id_market_chart`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-market-chart). Use it when you have an address rather than a CoinGecko id. For an explicit start and end use [`get_coingecko_token_market_chart_range`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-contract-contract-address-market-chart-range).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

[Set this endpoint up in your agent →](https://aisa.one/mcp?from=/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-contract-contract-address-market-chart)

# Coin Historical Chart Data by ID

> Price, market cap and volume history for one coin over a trailing window of days.

Historical series for one coin over a trailing window set by `days`, returned as three parallel arrays: `prices`, `market_caps` and `total_volumes`. Each entry is a two-element pair of timestamp and value, and the timestamp is in milliseconds. Granularity follows `days` automatically, or force it with `interval` (`daily` or `hourly`). Use it to chart a trend ending now. For an explicit start and end use [`get_coingecko_coins_id_market_chart_range`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-market-chart-range); for candlesticks use [`get_coingecko_coins_id_ohlc`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-ohlc); for one specific past day use [`get_coingecko_coins_id_history`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-history).

# Coin Historical Data by ID

> A one-day snapshot of a coin's price, market cap and volume for a specific calendar date.

A snapshot of one coin on a single calendar day. `date` is required and must be formatted dd-mm-yyyy (day, month, four-digit year). Returns `market_data` holding `current_price`, `market_cap` and `total_volume` as of that day, alongside `community_data`, `developer_data` and `public_interest_stats`. # Coin Historical Chart Data within Time Range by ID

> Historical series for one coin between two explicit timestamps — note seconds in, milliseconds out.

Historical series for one coin between two explicit points in time. `from` and `to` are Unix timestamps in seconds, while the timestamps inside the response are in milliseconds — the two are not the same unit, which is the usual source of empty or misaligned results. Returns `prices`, `market_caps` and `total_volumes` as timestamp-and-value pairs; CoinGecko picks granularity from the window length. Use it to line a series up with a known event window. For a trailing window ending now, [`get_coingecko_coins_id_market_chart`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-market-chart) takes a `days` count instead.

> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,

# Coin Historical Chart Data within Time Range by ID

> Historical series for one coin between two explicit timestamps — note seconds in, milliseconds out.

Historical series for one coin between two explicit points in time. `from` and `to` are Unix timestamps in seconds, while the timestamps inside the response are in milliseconds — the two are not the same unit, which is the usual source of empty or misaligned results. Returns `prices`, `market_caps` and `total_volumes` as timestamp-and-value pairs; CoinGecko picks granularity from the window length. Use it to line a series up with a known event window. For a trailing window ending now, [`get_coingecko_coins_id_market_chart`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-market-chart) takes a `days` count instead.

# Coin Price by Token Addresses

> Price lookup by on-chain contract address when you have a token address and no CoinGecko id.

Price lookup keyed by on-chain contract address rather than CoinGecko id. `id` is the asset platform, `contract_addresses` a comma-separated list of token addresses, `vs_currencies` the quote currency. Returns a map keyed by lowercase contract address whose field names are built from the quote currency — `usd`, plus `usd_market_cap`, `usd_24h_vol`, `usd_24h_change` and `last_updated_at` when the matching `include_market_cap`, `include_24hr_vol`, `include_24hr_change` and `include_last_updated_at` flags are set. # Coin Tickers by ID

> Every trading pair for one coin across venues, with prices, volumes, spreads and order-book depth.

Every trading pair for one coin across venues: `base`, `target`, `market`, `last`, `volume`, `converted_last`, `converted_volume`, `trust_score`, `bid_ask_spread_percentage`, `last_traded_at`, `trade_url`, and the anomaly flags `is_anomaly` and `is_stale`. Setting `depth` adds `cost_to_move_up_usd` and `cost_to_move_down_usd`. Narrow with `exchange_ids`, page with `page`, sort with `order` (trust score or volume). Use it to compare where one asset trades and how deep each book is. For every pair on one venue regardless of coin, use [`get_coingecko_exchanges_id_tickers`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-exchanges-id-tickers).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

# Coin Tickers by ID

> Every trading pair for one coin across venues, with prices, volumes, spreads and order-book depth.

Every trading pair for one coin across venues: `base`, `target`, `market`, `last`, `volume`, `converted_last`, `converted_volume`, `trust_score`, `bid_ask_spread_percentage`, `last_traded_at`, `trade_url`, and the anomaly flags `is_anomaly` and `is_stale`. Setting `depth` adds `cost_to_move_up_usd` and `cost_to_move_down_usd`. Narrow with `exchange_ids`, page with `page`, sort with `order` (trust score or volume). Use it to compare where one asset trades and how deep each book is. For every pair on one venue regardless of coin, use [`get_coingecko_exchanges_id_tickers`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-exchanges-id-tickers).

# Coins List with Market Data

> A ranked market table across many coins — price, market cap, volume, supply and all-time highs in one call.

A ranked market table covering many coins in one call: one row per coin with `current_price`, `market_cap`, `market_cap_rank`, `total_volume`, `high_24h`, `low_24h`, `price_change_percentage_24h`, `circulating_supply`, `total_supply`, `max_supply`, `ath` and `atl` with their dates, and `image`. Page with `per_page` and `page`, sort with `order` (market cap, volume or id, ascending or descending), and narrow with `ids` or `category`. Passing `price_change_percentage` adds a matching `price_change_percentage_24h_in_currency` field. Use it for leaderboards and segment scans. For the price of a few known coins [`get_coingecko_simple_price`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-simple-price) is far lighter; for one coin in full use [`get_coingecko_coins_id`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id).

> The full profile of one exchange: trust score, volume, coverage, social links and a ticker sample.

The full profile of one exchange: `name`, `year_established`, `country`, `description`, `url`, `image`, social handles, `centralized`, `trust_score`, `trust_score_rank`, `trade_volume_24h_btc`, `coins`, `pairs`, plus an embedded `tickers` sample and `status_updates`. # Exchange Data by ID

> The full profile of one exchange: trust score, volume, coverage, social links and a ticker sample.

The full profile of one exchange: `name`, `year_established`, `country`, `description`, `url`, `image`, social handles, `centralized`, `trust_score`, `trust_score_rank`, `trade_volume_24h_btc`, `coins`, `pairs`, plus an embedded `tickers` sample and `status_updates`. # Exchange Tickers by ID

> Every trading pair listed on one exchange, paged, with prices, volumes, spreads and depth.

Every trading pair listed on one exchange, paged: `base`, `target`, `market`, `last`, `volume`, `converted_last`, `converted_volume`, `trust_score`, `bid_ask_spread_percentage`, `timestamp`, `trade_url` and the `is_anomaly` / `is_stale` flags. Narrow to specific assets with `coin_ids`, sort with `order`, and set `depth` to add order-book move costs. Use it to audit one venue's coverage or liquidity. For one coin's pairs across all venues use [`get_coingecko_coins_id_tickers`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-tickers) instead.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

[Set this endpoint up in your agent →](https://aisa.one/mcp?from=/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-exchanges-id-tickers)

# Exchange Tickers by ID

> Every trading pair listed on one exchange, paged, with prices, volumes, spreads and depth.

Every trading pair listed on one exchange, paged: `base`, `target`, `market`, `last`, `volume`, `converted_last`, `converted_volume`, `trust_score`, `bid_ask_spread_percentage`, `timestamp`, `trade_url` and the `is_anomaly` / `is_stale` flags. Narrow to specific assets with `coin_ids`, sort with `order`, and set `depth` to add order-book move costs. Use it to audit one venue's coverage or liquidity. For one coin's pairs across all venues use [`get_coingecko_coins_id_tickers`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-id-tickers) instead.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

# Exchanges List with Data

> A paged directory of active exchanges with trust scores, ranks and 24h volume.

A paged directory of active exchanges with `id`, `name`, `year_established`, `country`, `description`, `url`, `image`, `trust_score`, `trust_score_rank`, `trade_volume_24h_btc` and `has_trading_incentive`. Quote the exact calls before running them (MCP `batch_quote`, CLI `aisa quote --json`). If the quote reports `auto_execute_eligible: true`, run it unless the user set a tighter limit or asked only for a quote. Otherwise, tell the user in one message the planned calls, the quoted price, and a total USD budget for the task, then wait for approval. Direct HTTP calls follow the stricter rule at https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/cli.md#direct-http-fallback. Do not make paid calls to test availability. Full rule: https://aisa.one/llms.txt

# Trending Search List

> What is trending on CoinGecko right now — 15 coins, 7 NFTs and 6 categories by search activity.

CoinGecko's current trending board, ranked by search activity on CoinGecko itself: `coins` (15 entries), `nfts` (7) and `categories` (6). Each coin carries `id`, `name`, `symbol`, `market_cap_rank`, `price_btc`, `score` and a nested `data` block. Takes no parameters. Use it as a discovery entry point when the user named no specific asset. It reflects attention rather than price action — for movers ranked by market data use [`get_coingecko_coins_markets`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/coingecko/get_coingecko-coins-markets) ordered by volume.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

> ## Agent Instructions
> - Base URLs: models `https://api.aisa.one/v1` (Gemini GenerateContent: `https://api.aisa.one/v1beta`); data APIs `https://api.aisa.one/apis/v1`. The `servers` of each operation in https://aisa.one/openapi.yaml is authoritative.

> - Spending: docs, https://aisa.one/models, https://aisa.one/api, `/v1/models`, and MCP `search`, `list_categories`, `get_details`, `batch_quote`, and the `account` operation are free. Quote the exact calls before running them (MCP `batch_quote`, CLI `aisa quote --json`). Otherwise, tell the user in one message the planned calls, the quoted price, and a total USD budget for the task, then wait for approval. # Billing & Credits

> How AIsa bills usage: one prepaid balance, per-token model pricing, fixed or metered data-API pricing, free quotes, spend caps, and per-call cost reporting. Current prices live on aisa.one/models and aisa.one/api.

AIsa is usage-based. You fund one balance and every model call, data-API call, MCP `batch_use`, and CLI `call` draws on it. You can pay as you go or choose a subscription plan; see [aisa.one/pricing](https://aisa.one/pricing) for plans.

The docs explain **how** you are billed. They do not list prices, which change more often than the docs. Current prices:

* **Models:** [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models) - input and output price per model, side by side.
* **Data APIs:** [aisa.one/api](https://aisa.one/api) - each provider page shows whether an endpoint is fixed or metered, its reference price, and its cost rules.

## Credits and top-ups

* New accounts start with free credit for testing.
* Top up in [Console → Billing](https://console.aisa.one/billing) (or `aisa topup` from the CLI). Payment completes on Stripe's hosted page.
* The balance is shared by all your keys and sessions. A key with a [spending limit](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/authentication.md#key-settings) can spend up to the lower of its remaining limit and the balance.
* When the balance or a key's limit runs out, requests fail with `402` (`insufficient_wallet_balance` or `insufficient_api_key_balance`) before any provider is called. A few premium endpoints also require a subscription; their `402` says so.

## Models

Model calls are billed by usage reported for that request:

| Model type | Billed by |
| - | - |
| Text, coding, and vision models | Per 1M tokens: input and output, plus cache read and cache write where the route reports them |
| Embedding, rerank, and classify models | Per 1M input tokens |
| Image models | Per request (one price however many images `n` asks for) or per token, depending on the model |
| Video models | Per second of output or per 1M tokens, with a separate rate per resolution |

For token models: `cost = input_tokens / 1,000,000 × input_price + output_tokens / 1,000,000 × output_price`, plus cache buckets when present. Streaming does not change the price. The response's `usage` object reports the tokens that were billed.

## Data APIs

Data APIs are billed per request under one of two models:

* **Fixed per call** - every successful request to the endpoint costs the same, regardless of response size. Examples: Open-Meteo, CoinGecko, Polymarket, Kalshi, Apollo, EDINET, FRED.
* **Metered** - the price follows what the request consumes (results, rows, pages, or provider credits), times your plan multiplier, so it grows with what the request returns. Examples: Twitter, Tavily, web search, Financial, YouTube, Scholar, Exa, Perplexity, Firecrawl, Semrush, Ahrefs, SimilarWeb, TikHub, DataForSEO.

Some endpoints, including SimilarWeb, use a credit formula. Read the endpoint's reference page for the formula before a paid request; if no maximum is documented, do not run it under an approval-first policy.

What counts as billable:

* A request that is processed and returns a result is billed. Each retry that succeeds is billed again, so make retries deliberate.
* A request rejected before processing - bad credentials, rate limiting, insufficient balance, a price above your cap - is not billed.
* Per-call rates can differ by plan or group; the amount actually applied is shown in Usage.

Through MCP, `search`, `list_categories`, `get_details`, and `batch_quote` are free; `batch_use` is billed per call at the same rates. Selected data endpoints also accept per-request payment through the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) without an API key; see [Machine Payments](https://aisa.one/docs/integrations/machine-payments.md).

## Cost estimates, quotes, and charges

* **Catalog estimates:** `default_request_estimate_usd` in the catalog describes a reference request. It is not a guaranteed starting price, a maximum, or a bill.
* **Free quotes:** On endpoints that support `X-AISA-Cost-Mode: quote`, send the exact request with the API key that will run it. The quote reflects your current account pricing. It does not call the upstream provider or debit your balance.
* **Account multiplier:** `billing_multiplier_ppm` is your multiplier in parts per million; divide by 1,000,000. For example, 1,000,000 means 1×. A published reference multiplier does not replace the one in your authenticated quote.
* **Micro-USD units:** Cost fields use integer micro-USD (1 USD = 1,000,000 micro-USD).
* **Settled cost:** After execution, the REST response header `X-AISA-Customer-Cost-Micros-USD`, or a successful native Tool result's `customer_cost_micros_usd`, reports the customer cost when present. Missing cost metadata means unknown, not free. A Tool `cost_estimate` is still an estimate, and provider cost is not your debit. Reconcile charges with [Usage](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/dashboard/overview.md#usage) and your balance; see the [API reference](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference.md#settled-call-cost) for parsing details.

## Quote, review, then execute

Use the complete URL and parameters from the current endpoint reference. The following GET example applies to endpoints that declare quote and maximum-price support. For POST or other methods, preserve the same method and body as well as the URL in both steps. Set `AISA_API_KEY` and `AISA_REQUEST_URL` in your environment; keep the same account and request parameters for both steps.

First, request a free quote:

```bash theme={null}
curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error "${AISA_REQUEST_URL:?Set AISA_REQUEST_URL}" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer ${AISA_API_KEY:?Set AISA_API_KEY}" \
  --header "X-AISA-Cost-Mode: quote" \
  --output quote.json
```

Check that the response has `object: cost_estimate`. Convert `estimated_cost_micros_usd` to USD by dividing by 1,000,000, without rounding down. Set `AISA_MAX_PRICE_USD` to the amount you approved. This is an admission check: if the execution estimate exceeds your limit, the gateway rejects the request with `402` before calling the upstream provider. It does not cap the final charge.

# Billing & Credits

> How AIsa bills usage: one prepaid balance, per-token model pricing, fixed or metered data-API pricing, free quotes, spend caps, and per-call cost reporting. Current prices live on aisa.one/models and aisa.one/api.

AIsa is usage-based. You fund one balance and every model call, data-API call, MCP `batch_use`, and CLI `call` draws on it. You can pay as you go or choose a subscription plan; see [aisa.one/pricing](https://aisa.one/pricing) for plans.

The docs explain **how** you are billed. They do not list prices, which change more often than the docs. Current prices:

* **Models:** [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models) - input and output price per model, side by side.
* **Data APIs:** [aisa.one/api](https://aisa.one/api) - each provider page shows whether an endpoint is fixed or metered, its reference price, and its cost rules.

## Credits and top-ups

* New accounts start with free credit for testing.
* Top up in [Console → Billing](https://console.aisa.one/billing) (or `aisa topup` from the CLI). Payment completes on Stripe's hosted page.
* The balance is shared by all your keys and sessions. A key with a [spending limit](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/authentication.md#key-settings) can spend up to the lower of its remaining limit and the balance.
* When the balance or a key's limit runs out, requests fail with `402` (`insufficient_wallet_balance` or `insufficient_api_key_balance`) before any provider is called. A few premium endpoints also require a subscription; their `402` says so.

## Models

Model calls are billed by usage reported for that request:

| Model type | Billed by |
| - | - |
| Text, coding, and vision models | Per 1M tokens: input and output, plus cache read and cache write where the route reports them |
| Embedding, rerank, and classify models | Per 1M input tokens |
| Image models | Per request or per generated image; some image models bill tokens plus per-image tiers |
| Video models | Per second of output or per 1M tokens, with a separate rate per resolution |

For token models: `cost = input_tokens / 1,000,000 × input_price + output_tokens / 1,000,000 × output_price`, plus cache buckets when present. Streaming does not change the price. The response's `usage` object reports the tokens that were billed.

## Data APIs

Data APIs are billed per request under one of two models:

* **Fixed per call** - every successful request to the endpoint costs the same, regardless of response size. Examples: Open-Meteo, CoinGecko, Polymarket, Kalshi, Apollo, EDINET, FRED.
* **Metered** - the price follows what the request consumes (results, rows, pages, or provider credits), times your plan multiplier, so it grows with what the request returns. Examples: Twitter, Tavily, web search, Financial, YouTube, Scholar, Exa, Perplexity, Firecrawl, Semrush, Ahrefs, SimilarWeb, TikHub, DataForSEO.

Some endpoints, including SimilarWeb, use a credit formula. Read the endpoint's reference page for the formula before a paid request; if no maximum is documented, do not run it under an approval-first policy.

What counts as billable:

* A request that is processed and returns a result is billed. Each retry that succeeds is billed again, so make retries deliberate.
* A request rejected before processing - bad credentials, rate limiting, insufficient balance, a price above your cap - is not billed.
* Per-call rates can differ by plan or group; the amount actually applied is shown in Usage.

Through MCP, `search`, `list_categories`, `get_details`, and `batch_quote` are free; `batch_use` is billed per call at the same rates. Selected data endpoints also accept per-request payment through the Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) without an API key; see [Machine Payments](https://aisa.one/docs/integrations/machine-payments.md).

## Cost estimates, quotes, and charges

* **Catalog estimates:** `default_request_estimate_usd` in the catalog describes a reference request. It is not a guaranteed starting price, a maximum, or a bill.
* **Free quotes:** On endpoints that support `X-AISA-Cost-Mode: quote`, send the exact request with the API key that will run it. The quote reflects your current account pricing. It does not call the upstream provider or debit your balance.
* **Account multiplier:** `billing_multiplier_ppm` is your multiplier in parts per million; divide by 1,000,000. For example, 1,000,000 means 1×. A published reference multiplier does not replace the one in your authenticated quote.
* **Micro-USD units:** Cost fields use integer micro-USD (1 USD = 1,000,000 micro-USD).
* **Settled cost:** After execution, the REST response header `X-AISA-Customer-Cost-Micros-USD`, or a successful native Tool result's `customer_cost_micros_usd`, reports the customer cost when present. Missing cost metadata means unknown, not free. A Tool `cost_estimate` is still an estimate, and provider cost is not your debit. # Email Lookup

> Contact emails for one TikTok, Instagram or YouTube creator, from a profile URL.

Looks up the contact email for one Instagram, TikTok or YouTube creator from a profile URL. Pass `profile_url`; the response returns the parsed `platform`, the normalized `profile_url`, and an `email` object shaped `{status, value}`.

A `not_found` status (with `value` null) is a normal result, not an error — the creator publishes no address — and is still billed as one valid lookup.

Handles one creator per call. To assemble a creator list first, use [`post_waveinflu_similar_creators`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/waveinflu/post_waveinflu-similar) or [`post_waveinflu_ai_search`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/waveinflu/post_waveinflu-ai-search) — each match already includes an `email` for most creators, so call this endpoint for the ones that come back null.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Breaking change (migration to hiCreator upstream).** The request field is now `profile_url` (previously `url`), and the response is `data.email.{status, value}` plus `data.profile_url`. The former `emails[]`, `contacts[]`, `username`, and `quota` fields have been removed. Sending the legacy `url` field returns `400 code=10001` and is not billed.

```bash REST theme={null}
  -d '{"profile_url": "https://www.instagram.com/onkimia/"}'
```

# Email Lookup

> Contact emails for one TikTok, Instagram or YouTube creator, from a profile URL.

Looks up the contact email for one Instagram, TikTok or YouTube creator from a profile URL. Pass `profile_url`; the response returns the parsed `platform`, the normalized `profile_url`, and an `email` object shaped `{status, value}`.

A `not_found` status (with `value` null) is a normal result, not an error — the creator publishes no address — and is still billed as one valid lookup.

Handles one creator per call. To assemble a creator list first, use [`post_waveinflu_similar_creators`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/waveinflu/post_waveinflu-similar) or [`post_waveinflu_ai_search`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/waveinflu/post_waveinflu-ai-search) — each match already includes an `email` for most creators, so call this endpoint for the ones that come back null.

The former `emails[]`, `contacts[]`, `username`, and `quota` fields have been removed. Sending the legacy `url` field returns `400 code=10001` and is not billed.
