# Similar Creators

> Find creators similar to a seed account on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube.

Finds creators similar to a seed account on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube. `platform` and `target_account` are required; add `limit` (1–100, default 25) and optional `filters` for regions, languages, follower and play-count ranges, gender, ethnicity, creator type, face visibility, and workspace deduplication.

Each match returns a rich profile: `id`, `username`, `fullName`, `biography`, `email`, `followerCount`, `averagePlayCount` / `medianPlayCount`, `averageEngagementRate` / `medianEngagementRate`, `region`, `language`, AI-inferred `gender`, `ageRange`, `ethnicity`, `faceVisibility`, `accountPositioning` tags, an `aiDescription`, `profileUrl`, and a relevance `score`. Results are sorted by `score` descending.

Prefer a natural-language brief over a seed account? Use [`post_waveinflu_ai_search`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/waveinflu/post_waveinflu-ai-search), which returns the same creator shape.

Most matches already include an `email`. Use [`post_waveinflu_email_lookup`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/waveinflu/post_waveinflu-email-lookup) for the ones that come back null.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Breaking change (migration to hiCreator upstream).** The seed is now a single required `target_account` (previously `seedProfileUrl` / `contentDirection`). The response is `data.items[]` with `data.count` (previously `data.data[]` with `total`), and each match uses `score` (previously `similarityScore`). The `mode`, `sourceUserId`, and `quota` fields have been removed, and new profile fields (`biography`, `gender`, `ageRange`, `ethnicity`, `faceVisibility`, `accountPositioning`, `aiDescription`) have been added. Billing is per delivered creator (`data.count`).

# Similar Creators

> Find creators similar to a seed account on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube.

Finds creators similar to a seed account on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube. `platform` and `target_account` are required; add `limit` (1–100, default 25) and optional `filters` for regions, languages, follower and play-count ranges, gender, ethnicity, creator type, face visibility, and workspace deduplication.

Each match returns a rich profile: `id`, `username`, `fullName`, `biography`, `email`, `followerCount`, `averagePlayCount` / `medianPlayCount`, `averageEngagementRate` / `medianEngagementRate`, `region`, `language`, AI-inferred `gender`, `ageRange`, `ethnicity`, `faceVisibility`, `accountPositioning` tags, an `aiDescription`, `profileUrl`, and a relevance `score`. Results are sorted by `score` descending.

Prefer a natural-language brief over a seed account? Use [`post_waveinflu_ai_search`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/waveinflu/post_waveinflu-ai-search), which returns the same creator shape.

Most matches already include an `email`. Use [`post_waveinflu_email_lookup`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/waveinflu/post_waveinflu-email-lookup) for the ones that come back null.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Breaking change (migration to hiCreator upstream).** The seed is now a single required `target_account` (previously `seedProfileUrl` / `contentDirection`). The response is `data.items[]` with `data.count` (previously `data.data[]` with `total`), and each match uses `score` (previously `similarityScore`). The `mode`, `sourceUserId`, and `quota` fields have been removed, and new profile fields (`biography`, `gender`, `ageRange`, `ethnicity`, `faceVisibility`, `accountPositioning`, `aiDescription`) have been added. Billing is per delivered creator (`data.count`).

# Connect your agent to AIsa

> Add the AIsa MCP server to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or other agents, sign in with browser OAuth, and start using tools. Use the CLI only when MCP cannot run.

**AI agent reading this?** Go to [Agent instructions](#agent-instructions) and run the setup yourself.

AIsa provides a remote MCP server at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp`. Authentication uses browser OAuth, so there is no API key to copy.

**1. Add the server**

```bash Claude Code theme={null}
claude mcp add --transport http -s user aisa https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp
```

```bash Codex theme={null}
codex mcp add aisa --url https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp
```

```json Cursor (~/.cursor/mcp.json) theme={null}
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "aisa": { "url": "https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp" }
  }
}
```

```json VS Code (.vscode/mcp.json) theme={null}
{
  "servers": {
    "aisa": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp" }
  }
}
```

For Claude: add a custom connector with `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` ([guide](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/tutorials/use-aisa-in-claude.md)). For ChatGPT: install the AIsa GTM plugin ([guide](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/tutorials/use-aisa-in-chatgpt.md)).

**2. Sign in**

Your MCP client opens a browser window; click **Allow** to complete OAuth. In Claude Code, run `/mcp`, select **aisa**, and authenticate. In Cursor, open **Customize** → **MCPs** and click **Authenticate** on **aisa**.

**3. Ask your agent**

Paste this into your agent chat:

```txt wrap theme={null}
Use AIsa to check my account, then find three recent public updates about a company of your choice with source links. Ask me before any paid call.
```

Prefer to let the agent do the setup too? Paste `Set up AIsa using https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md.` and it follows the instructions below.

## Agent instructions

Set up AIsa. Run the matching commands yourself. Do not ask the user to run them — except when a sandbox or a denied write blocks you: then relay the exact steps and wait.

Reuse a working connection: an authorized AIsa MCP server at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` whose tool list includes `search` and `batch_quote`, or an official `aisa` skill plus valid CLI auth. Explicit choice or a still-authorized connection wins; do not migrate or reinstall automatically. Do not change unrelated model settings. Describe installs and credentials as in this agent environment.

Default to native remote MCP at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth) whenever this client can add that connector — user-local or cloud, with or without a terminal. A working shell is not a reason to choose the CLI.

Use the CLI only when this client has no MCP mechanism at all, or by explicit user choice. A client without a browser (CI, SSH, container) still uses MCP, with an API key instead of OAuth. These gates and the Node rule in [Use the CLI](https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/cli.md) take precedence over any installed `aisa` skill; the skill covers follow-up operations only.

### MCP (default)

Connect `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). No CLI, npm, npx, or Skill install is required; already-installed guidance may be used. The client owns browser sign-in and tokens. Use this client's own MCP mechanism, not a hand-edited config file of another tool:

* Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http -s user aisa https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp`
* Codex: `codex mcp add aisa --url https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` (Codex starts OAuth on its own)
* Cursor / VS Code: a `url` entry for `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` in the MCP config

If this client cannot open a browser (CI, SSH, container), send `Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY` instead of OAuth (Claude Code: `--header "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY"`; Codex: `--bearer-token-env-var AISA_API_KEY`). If `AISA_API_KEY` is not set, ask the user to create a key at [console.aisa.one/api-keys](https://console.aisa.one/api-keys) and set it in the environment; never ask them to paste it into chat. Never print, log, or commit the key.

Add the connector, then let the user finish OAuth in the browser (skip this when the client sends `AISA_API_KEY`). If this client supports MCP but you cannot add the connector from here — unknown capability, sandbox, or permission denied — do not switch to the CLI: ask the user to enable or add the connector, then wait. If the client must reload or start a new session to load the connector, tell the user; verify the tools afterwards, and do not switch to the CLI meanwhile.

Grok Bot + Plugins: Settings → Plugins → Add → auth if asked → `@` attach. If a native custom MCP setup exists, enter that URL and complete OAuth. If neither is available, ask the user to enable or add the connector. grok.com (`grok.com/connectors`) is a different product.

Then work with those tools: `search` (describe the task; reuse its `session_id`) → `get_details` (also served as `batch_get_schema`) when a result lacks the full schema → `batch_quote` with the exact calls → `batch_use` with the same calls, up to 20 per batch. `search`, `list_categories`, `get_details`, and `batch_quote` are free; `batch_use` is billed per call. `use` is the older single-call form, kept for existing clients; here it is only needed for the free `account` check below. Take tool names and arguments from `search` or `get_details`; do not invent names or prices. Spending approval and error handling (`401`, `402`, `429`) follow sections 4 and 5 of [the agent setup guide](https://aisa.one/llms.txt).

### CLI (only when MCP cannot run here)

Follow [Use the CLI](https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/cli.md): its gate, Node.js rule, skill install, and sign-in. Do not work around a missing prerequisite or a denied write.

### Finish

**AIsa is connected.** only after valid authentication (OAuth, or the existing `AISA_API_KEY` sent as a Bearer token) plus a successful free protected call — MCP `use` with `operation_id` `account`, which returns the key, balance, and usage — or `aisa balance` (CLI). Tool metadata or a `401` is not a protected call. A missing connector is not connected. Then continue a named task, or ask **What would you like to do first?** CLI follows the `aisa` skill; MCP uses those tools. Setup is not spend approval.

Do not jump to HTTP to bypass missing credentials, exhausted credit, or the same API outage. Do not make paid calls to test availability. Do not extract client-owned MCP OAuth tokens.

Only if CLI and MCP are both unavailable, HTTP works, and a valid AIsa key already exists: read the direct HTTP section of [Use the CLI](https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/cli.md#direct-http-fallback) (endpoint docs, pricing, approval XML) before a paid proposal, cost approval, or paid request. Extra models, REST, keys, or skills: [AIsa docs](https://aisa.one/docs).

# List markets

> List individual Polymarket prediction markets — one binary question each — with live pricing.

List individual Polymarket prediction markets — one binary question each — with live pricing. Use this when you need the market-implied probability of a specific outcome, or to screen markets by size and timing; filter with `slug`, `condition_ids`, `clob_token_ids`, `tag_id`, `closed`, and the `volume_num_*` / `start_date_*` / `end_date_*` ranges.

Returns a top-level array of market objects. The probability signal is `outcomes` paired with `outcomePrices`, quoted against `bestBid` / `bestAsk`; `conditionId` and `clobTokenIds` are the on-chain identifiers you need to join to other Polymarket data.

For the topic that groups several related questions together, use [`get_polymarket_events`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/prediction-market/get_polymarket-events). For the same kind of question on the US-regulated Kalshi exchange, use [`get_kalshi_markets`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/prediction-market/get_kalshi-markets).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

[Set this endpoint up in your agent →](https://aisa.one/mcp?from=/api-reference/prediction-market/get_polymarket-markets)

      "in": "query",

# List markets

> List individual Polymarket prediction markets — one binary question each — with live pricing.

List individual Polymarket prediction markets — one binary question each — with live pricing. Use this when you need the market-implied probability of a specific outcome, or to screen markets by size and timing; filter with `slug`, `condition_ids`, `clob_token_ids`, `tag_id`, `closed`, and the `volume_num_*` / `start_date_*` / `end_date_*` ranges.

Returns a top-level array of market objects. The probability signal is `outcomes` paired with `outcomePrices`, quoted against `bestBid` / `bestAsk`; `conditionId` and `clobTokenIds` are the on-chain identifiers you need to join to other Polymarket data.

For the topic that groups several related questions together, use [`get_polymarket_events`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/prediction-market/get_polymarket-events). For the same kind of question on the US-regulated Kalshi exchange, use [`get_kalshi_markets`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/prediction-market/get_kalshi-markets).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

> ## Agent Instructions
> - Base URLs: models `https://api.aisa.one/v1` (Gemini GenerateContent: `https://api.aisa.one/v1beta`); data APIs `https://api.aisa.one/apis/v1`. The `servers` of each operation in https://aisa.one/openapi.yaml is authoritative.
> - Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY`. Never print, log, or commit the key.
> - MCP (preferred for agents): `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp`, signed in with OAuth, so there is no key to paste.
> - Agent Skill: `npx skills add AIsa-team/agent-skills --skill aisa`. Fallback with the AIsa CLI: `aisa skills install aisa`.
> - Spending: docs, https://aisa.one/models, https://aisa.one/api, `/v1/models`, and MCP `search`, `list_categories`, `get_details`, `batch_quote`, and the `account` operation are free. Quote the exact calls before running them (MCP `batch_quote`, CLI `aisa quote --json`). If the quote reports `auto_execute_eligible: true`, run it unless the user set a tighter limit or asked only for a quote. Otherwise, tell the user in one message the planned calls, the quoted price, and a total USD budget for the task, then wait for approval. Direct HTTP calls follow the stricter rule at https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/cli.md#direct-http-fallback. Do not make paid calls to test availability. Full rule: https://aisa.one/llms.txt

# Search Videos

> Search YouTube and get back matching videos, channels, and playlists.

Search YouTube and get back matching videos, channels, and playlists. Set `engine=youtube` and pass the query in `q`; both are required. Optionally narrow by country (`gl`) and interface language (`hl`), or pass a YouTube filter token in `sp` for pagination and advanced filters such as upload date, duration, or result type. Use this to find video content on a topic, track a channel's recent uploads, or gauge how much video coverage a subject has.

Note: this is served through the AIsa mapped path `/apis/v1/youtube/search`; the upstream provider's canonical path is not mounted directly.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

[Set this endpoint up in your agent →](https://aisa.one/mcp?from=/api-reference/search/get_youtube-search)

# Search Videos

> Search YouTube and get back matching videos, channels, and playlists.

Search YouTube and get back matching videos, channels, and playlists. Set `engine=youtube` and pass the query in `q`; both are required. Optionally narrow by country (`gl`) and interface language (`hl`), or pass a YouTube filter token in `sp` for pagination and advanced filters such as upload date, duration, or result type. Use this to find video content on a topic, track a channel's recent uploads, or gauge how much video coverage a subject has.

Note: this is served through the AIsa mapped path `/apis/v1/youtube/search`; the upstream provider's canonical path is not mounted directly.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

> ## Documentation Index

> ## Agent Instructions
> - Base URLs: models `https://api.aisa.one/v1` (Gemini GenerateContent: `https://api.aisa.one/v1beta`); data APIs `https://api.aisa.one/apis/v1`. The `servers` of each operation in https://aisa.one/openapi.yaml is authoritative.
> - Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY`. Never print, log, or commit the key.
> - MCP (preferred for agents): `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp`, signed in with OAuth, so there is no key to paste.
> - Agent Skill: `npx skills add AIsa-team/agent-skills --skill aisa`. Fallback with the AIsa CLI: `aisa skills install aisa`.
> - Spending: docs, https://aisa.one/models, https://aisa.one/api, `/v1/models`, and MCP `search`, `list_categories`, `get_details`, `batch_quote`, and the `account` operation are free. Quote the exact calls before running them (MCP `batch_quote`, CLI `aisa quote --json`). If the quote reports `auto_execute_eligible: true`, run it unless the user set a tighter limit or asked only for a quote. Otherwise, tell the user in one message the planned calls, the quoted price, and a total USD budget for the task, then wait for approval. Direct HTTP calls follow the stricter rule at https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/cli.md#direct-http-fallback. Do not make paid calls to test availability. Full rule: https://aisa.one/llms.txt

# Search Tavily Data

> Search the web and get back ranked results with the page text already extracted, so there is no second call to fetch content.

Search the web and get back ranked results with the page text already extracted, so there is no second call to fetch content. `query` is required. Returns `results[]` with `url`, `title`, `content` (the extracted excerpt), `score` and optionally `raw_content`, alongside `query`, `images`, `response_time` and `request_id`; set `include_answer` to also get a one-paragraph `answer`. Filter with `topic` (general/news/finance), `time_range` or explicit `start_date`/`end_date`, and trade cost against depth with `search_depth`. Measured at roughly 6 seconds for 2 results. This is the default choice for open-web research, and the only search here that returns ranked results and page text in one call. Reach past it when: you already know the URLs — [`post_tavily_extract`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/search/post_tavily-extract) is cheaper and exact; the query is a description rather than keywords — `post_exa_search` matches on meaning; you want a written answer rather than a list to iterate — [`post_perplexity_sonar`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/perplexity/post_perplexity-sonar); you want peer-reviewed papers — [`post_scholar_search_scholar`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/scholar/post_scholar-search-scholar).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

[Set this endpoint up in your agent →](https://aisa.one/mcp?from=/api-reference/search/post_tavily-search)

# Advanced Search

> Search X posts by keyword or query with X's advanced search operators, sorted by Latest (default) or Top.

Search X posts by keyword or query with X's advanced search operators, sorted by Latest (default) or Top. This is the primary entry point for X content research when you do not yet have tweet IDs or handles. Supports operators in the query string such as `from:`, `to:`, `since:`, `until:`, `min_faves:`, and `-filter:replies`. Cursor-paginated; returns tweets with `has_next_page` and `next_cursor`.

To search accounts rather than posts use [`get_twitter_user_search`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/twitter/get_twitter-user-search).

To read one account's own posts use [`get_twitter_user_tweet_timeline`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/twitter/get_twitter-user-tweet-timeline).

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call

# Advanced Search

> Search X posts by keyword or query with X's advanced search operators, sorted by Latest (default) or Top.

Search X posts by keyword or query with X's advanced search operators, sorted by Latest (default) or Top. This is the primary entry point for X content research when you do not yet have tweet IDs or handles. Supports operators in the query string such as `from:`, `to:`, `since:`, `until:`, `min_faves:`, and `-filter:replies`. Cursor-paginated; returns tweets with `has_next_page` and `next_cursor`.

To search accounts rather than posts use [`get_twitter_user_search`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/twitter/get_twitter-user-search).

To read one account's own posts use [`get_twitter_user_tweet_timeline`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/twitter/get_twitter-user-tweet-timeline).

> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call

# AIsa Model Catalog: Model IDs, Routes, and Capabilities

> Find current AIsa model IDs, supported endpoints, and capabilities via GET /v1/models or the live catalog at aisa.one/models.

AIsa routes LLM, image, video, and embedding models through a single API key. Because models are frequently added and retired, this page explains how to query the catalog dynamically rather than maintaining a static list.

> [card] [GET /v1/models](#list-models-with-the-api)
>
> Machine-readable list of model IDs, routes, and capability tags for applications and agents.

> [card] [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models)
>
> Browse, filter, and compare models, with current prices.

## List models with the API

Send your API key as a Bearer token. Listing models is free; requests without an API key return `402`.

```bash theme={null}
curl https://api.aisa.one/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY"
```

The response follows the standard OpenAI list format, extended with an `aisa` metadata object for each model:

```json theme={null}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "claude-fable-5-1",
      "object": "model",
      "created": 1788315984,
      "owned_by": "Anthropic",
      "aisa": {
        "display_name": "claude-fable-5-1",
        "model_type": "text",
        "capabilities": ["chat", "long-context", "reasoning", "tools"],
        "preferred_route": "anthropic",
        "routes": [
          { "key": "openai", "path": "/v1/chat/completions", "method": "POST" },
          { "key": "anthropic", "path": "/v1/messages", "method": "POST", "preferred": true }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `id` | The exact string to pass as `model`. |
| `owned_by` | Upstream provider, such as `OpenAI`, `Anthropic`, or `Alibaba`. |
| `aisa.model_type` | `text`, `image`, `video`, or `embedding`. |
| `aisa.capabilities` | Capability tags, such as `chat`, `tools`, `reasoning`, `vision`, `image`, `videos`, or `embeddings`. |
| `aisa.routes` | Every AIsa endpoint serving this model, specified as `method` + `path`. |
| `aisa.preferred_route` | Present on some models. The `key` of the recommended route (which also has `"preferred": true`). |

Filter the list with `jq`:

```bash theme={null}
# Models served by the Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoint
curl -s https://api.aisa.one/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.data[] | select(any(.aisa.routes[]; .path == "/v1/messages")) | .id'

# Image models
curl -s https://api.aisa.one/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aisa.model_type == "image") | .id'
```

## Endpoints by model type

| Model type | Endpoints | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| Text | `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `POST /v1/messages`, `POST /v1/responses` | Most text models serve both OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible routes. Check `routes` before switching protocols. |
| Image | `POST /v1/images/generations`, `POST /v1/images/edits` | Not every image model supports edits. |
| Video | `POST /v1/video/generations`, then `GET /v1/video/generations/{task_id}` | Asynchronous: submit a job, then poll for the result. |
| Embedding | `POST /v1/embeddings` | |

Calling a model on an unsupported route returns `400` with `error.code` set to `model_route_not_supported`; `error.supported_routes` lists the routes that work. Request and response schemas for each endpoint are documented in the [API Reference](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/chat/post_chat-completions.md).

## Call a model

Point any OpenAI-compatible SDK at `https://api.aisa.one/v1` and pass a model `id` from the catalog:

```python theme={null}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key="YOUR_AISA_API_KEY", base_url="https://api.aisa.one/v1")

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen3.7-max",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Compare these model options for a coding agent."}],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

For the Anthropic SDK and other clients, see [OpenAI / Anthropic SDK](https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/sdk-compatibility.md).

## Browse and compare on aisa.one

For interactive browsing, visit [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models). You can search by model, provider, or endpoint, filter by provider and capability, and compare models side by side. It also displays each model's current price, which these docs do not list.

## How models are billed

Models draw on the same prepaid balance as data APIs. The billing unit depends on the model:

* **Text and embedding models:** Billed per token, with separate rates for input and output, and for cache reads or writes where caching is supported.
* **Image models:** Billed per request or per token, depending on the model. A per-request model charges one price however many images `n` asks for.
* **Video models:** Billed per output second or per token, by resolution.

The live catalog shows each model's billing type and current price. The final charge for each call is recorded in your usage logs. See [Billing & Credits](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/pricing.md) for balances, spend limits, and quotes.

## Chinese models

Qwen, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, ByteDance Seed, MiniMax, and other Chinese models use the same endpoints. See [Chinese AI Models](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/chinese-llms.md) for per-family guides.

## Notes for agents

* Use only model IDs dynamically returned by `GET /v1/models`. Do not guess model IDs or reuse them from memory.
* Select the endpoint from the model's `routes` list; prioritize the route marked `"preferred": true` when present.
* Do not assume a model supports a modality simply because its upstream family does. Always check `model_type` and `capabilities`.
* Listing models via `GET /v1/models` is free and allowed before the user approves any spend. Current prices are listed on [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models), not in these docs.

# Sonar Deep Research

> Commission a report: this endpoint runs many searches and writes a long, cited document.

Commission a report: this endpoint runs many searches and writes a long, cited document. `model` (required, `sonar-deep-research`) and `messages` in; `choices[0].message.content`, `citations`, `search_results[]` and `usage` out, where `usage` also reports `num_search_queries` and `reasoning_tokens`. ⚠️ Budget for the wait: a two-sentence question measured **192 seconds** and returned 86 KB after 10 upstream searches — roughly 60 times slower and 10 times larger than [`post_perplexity_sonar`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/perplexity/post_perplexity-sonar), at the same flat per-request rate. Many clients time out well before it answers, so call it only when a report is genuinely the deliverable, and never in a loop. For anything you would read in one sitting, the other three Perplexity endpoints answer in seconds.

## Example

```bash REST theme={null}
curl -X POST "https://api.aisa.one/apis/v1/perplexity/sonar-deep-research" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "sonar-deep-research",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Write a comprehensive analysis of the global semiconductor supply chain risks in 2026"}
    ]
  }'
```

```jsonc MCP theme={null}
// Copy this whole block into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any coding agent.
// It carries everything needed to connect, authorize and run this example —
// no key to paste, one click of Allow in the browser.
{
  "calls": [
    {
      "call_id": "1",
      "tool": "post_perplexity_sonar_deep_research",
      "arguments": {
        "model": "sonar-deep-research",
        "messages": [
          {
            "role": "user",
            "content": "Write a comprehensive analysis of the global semiconductor supply chain risks in 2026"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
// ── for the agent ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Register the AIsa MCP server, then call its `batch_quote` tool with the JSON above.
//   name       aisa
//   endpoint   https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp
//   transport  streamable-http
//   auth       OAuth. The server publishes RFC 9728 metadata, so open a
//              browser and the user clicks Allow once — nothing to paste.
//              If AISA_API_KEY is set, send it as a bearer header instead.
// Use your own MCP mechanism, not a hand-edited config file:
//   Codex        codex mcp add aisa --url https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp
//   Claude Code  claude mcp add --transport http -s user aisa https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp
//   Cursor / VS Code   a "url" entry for https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp in the MCP config
// The server reaches https://mcp.aisa.one/servers worth of APIs through a few meta
// tools: search, list_categories, get_details, batch_quote, batch_use.
// search, get_details and batch_quote are free; batch_use is billed per
// call. This operation's full contract — every argument, the response
// shape, the price and the pitfalls — is at
//   https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/perplexity/post_perplexity-sonar-deep-research.md
// Show me the quoted cost. Once I approve, run the same calls with
// batch_use and show me the result.
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> **First time?** Point any MCP client at `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp` — Claude
> Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. Authorization is OAuth: the client
> opens a browser, you click Allow once, and there is no key to paste. Your
> agent then reaches every endpoint through a few meta tools: `search`,
> `list_categories`, `get_details` and `batch_quote` are free, `batch_use` is
> billed per call. Setup per client is in
> [Connect via MCP](https://aisa.one/docs/agent-quickstart.md); the live tool list and what each call
> costs are on [aisa.one/mcp](https://aisa.one/mcp#connect).

# Sonar Pro

> Ask a question that needs more than one search pass and get a written answer with citations.

Ask a question that needs more than one search pass and get a written answer with citations. Same request and response shape as [`post_perplexity_sonar`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/perplexity/post_perplexity-sonar) — `model` (required, `sonar-pro`) and `messages` in, `choices[0].message.content`, `citations`, `search_results[]` and `usage` out. Ask a question that has to be worked through, not just looked up, and get a step-by-step answer backed by web search. # Sonar

> Ask a question and get a written answer with web citations, rather than a list of links to read yourself.

Ask a question and get a written answer with web citations, rather than a list of links to read yourself. Body is OpenAI chat-completions shaped: `model` (required, `sonar`) and `messages`. Returns `choices[0].message.content` as prose, plus `citations` (an array of URL strings) and `search_results[]` with `title`, `url`, `snippet`, `date` and `source`, and a `usage` block. Measured at about 3 seconds. Billed at a flat rate per request. This is the cheapest and fastest of the four Perplexity endpoints — use it for a single factual question. Step up to [`post_perplexity_sonar_pro`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/perplexity/post_perplexity-sonar-pro) for multi-part questions, or [`post_perplexity_sonar_reasoning_pro`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/perplexity/post_perplexity-sonar-reasoning-pro) when the answer requires working through steps. If you need results you can iterate over rather than prose, use [`post_tavily_search`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/search/post_tavily-search); `post_exa_answer` answers the same shape of question with semantic retrieval.

# Sonar

> Ask a question and get a written answer with web citations, rather than a list of links to read yourself.

Ask a question and get a written answer with web citations, rather than a list of links to read yourself. Body is OpenAI chat-completions shaped: `model` (required, `sonar`) and `messages`. Returns `choices[0].message.content` as prose, plus `citations` (an array of URL strings) and `search_results[]` with `title`, `url`, `snippet`, `date` and `source`, and a `usage` block. Measured at about 3 seconds. Billed at a flat rate per request. This is the cheapest and fastest of the four Perplexity endpoints — use it for a single factual question. Step up to [`post_perplexity_sonar_pro`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/perplexity/post_perplexity-sonar-pro) for multi-part questions, or [`post_perplexity_sonar_reasoning_pro`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/perplexity/post_perplexity-sonar-reasoning-pro) when the answer requires working through steps. If you need results you can iterate over rather than prose, use [`post_tavily_search`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/search/post_tavily-search); `post_exa_answer` answers the same shape of question with semantic retrieval.

optional field

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://aisa.one/docs/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

> ## Agent Instructions
> - Base URLs: models `https://api.aisa.one/v1` (Gemini GenerateContent: `https://api.aisa.one/v1beta`); data APIs `https://api.aisa.one/apis/v1`. The `servers` of each operation in https://aisa.one/openapi.yaml is authoritative.
> - Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY`. Never print, log, or commit the key.
> - MCP (preferred for agents): `https://mcp.aisa.one/mcp`, signed in with OAuth, so there is no key to paste.
> - Agent Skill: `npx skills add AIsa-team/agent-skills --skill aisa`. Fallback with the AIsa CLI: `aisa skills install aisa`.
> - Spending: docs, https://aisa.one/models, https://aisa.one/api, `/v1/models`, and MCP `search`, `list_categories`, `get_details`, `batch_quote`, and the `account` operation are free. Quote the exact calls before running them (MCP `batch_quote`, CLI `aisa quote --json`). If the quote reports `auto_execute_eligible: true`, run it unless the user set a tighter limit or asked only for a quote. Otherwise, tell the user in one message the planned calls, the quoted price, and a total USD budget for the task, then wait for approval. Direct HTTP calls follow the stricter rule at https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/cli.md#direct-http-fallback. Do not make paid calls to test availability. Full rule: https://aisa.one/llms.txt

# AIsa Model Catalog: Model IDs, Routes, and Capabilities

> Find current AIsa model IDs, supported endpoints, and capabilities via GET /v1/models or the live catalog at aisa.one/models.

AIsa routes LLM, image, video, and embedding models through a single API key. Because models are frequently added and retired, this page explains how to query the catalog dynamically rather than maintaining a static list.

> [card] [GET /v1/models](#list-models-with-the-api)
>
> Machine-readable list of model IDs, routes, and capability tags for applications and agents.

> [card] [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models)
>
> Browse, filter, and compare models, with current prices.

## List models with the API

Send your API key as a Bearer token. Listing models is free; requests without an API key return `402`.

```bash theme={null}
curl https://api.aisa.one/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY"
```

The response follows the standard OpenAI list format, extended with an `aisa` metadata object for each model:

```json theme={null}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "claude-fable-5-1",
      "object": "model",
      "created": 1788315984,
      "owned_by": "Anthropic",
      "aisa": {
        "display_name": "claude-fable-5-1",
        "model_type": "text",
        "capabilities": ["chat", "long-context", "reasoning", "tools"],
        "preferred_route": "anthropic",
        "routes": [
          { "key": "openai", "path": "/v1/chat/completions", "method": "POST" },
          { "key": "anthropic", "path": "/v1/messages", "method": "POST", "preferred": true }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `id` | The exact string to pass as `model`. |
| `owned_by` | Upstream provider, such as `OpenAI`, `Anthropic`, or `Alibaba`. |
| `aisa.model_type` | `text`, `image`, `video`, or `embedding`. |
| `aisa.capabilities` | Capability tags, such as `chat`, `tools`, `reasoning`, `vision`, `image`, `videos`, or `embeddings`. |
| `aisa.routes` | Every AIsa endpoint serving this model, specified as `method` + `path`. |
| `aisa.preferred_route` | Present on some models. The `key` of the recommended route (which also has `"preferred": true`). |

Filter the list with `jq`:

```bash theme={null}
# Models served by the Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoint
curl -s https://api.aisa.one/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.data[] | select(any(.aisa.routes[]; .path == "/v1/messages")) | .id'

# Image models
curl -s https://api.aisa.one/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aisa.model_type == "image") | .id'
```

## Endpoints by model type

| Model type | Endpoints | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| Text | `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `POST /v1/messages`, `POST /v1/responses` | Most text models serve both OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible routes. Check `routes` before switching protocols. |
| Image | `POST /v1/images/generations`, `POST /v1/images/edits` | Not every image model supports edits. |
| Video | `POST /v1/video/generations`, then `GET /v1/video/generations/{task_id}` | Asynchronous: submit a job, then poll for the result. |
| Embedding | `POST /v1/embeddings` | |

Calling a model on an unsupported route returns `400` with `error.code` set to `model_route_not_supported`; `error.supported_routes` lists the routes that work. Request and response schemas for each endpoint are documented in the [API Reference](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/chat/post_chat-completions.md).

## Call a model

Point any OpenAI-compatible SDK at `https://api.aisa.one/v1` and pass a model `id` from the catalog:

```python theme={null}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key="YOUR_AISA_API_KEY", base_url="https://api.aisa.one/v1")

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen3.7-max",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Compare these model options for a coding agent."}],
)
print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

For the Anthropic SDK and other clients, see [OpenAI / Anthropic SDK](https://aisa.one/docs/get-started/sdk-compatibility.md).

## Browse and compare on aisa.one

For interactive browsing, visit [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models). You can search by model, provider, or endpoint, filter by provider and capability, and compare models side by side. It also displays each model's current price, which these docs do not list.

## How models are billed

Models draw on the same prepaid balance as data APIs. The billing unit depends on the model:

* **Text and embedding models:** Billed per token, with separate rates for input and output, and for cache reads or writes where caching is supported.
* **Image models:** Billed per request or per token, depending on the model. A per-request model charges one price however many images `n` asks for.
* **Video models:** Billed per output second or per token, by resolution.

The live catalog shows each model's billing type and current price. The final charge for each call is recorded in your usage logs. See [Billing & Credits](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/pricing.md) for balances, spend limits, and quotes.

* Use only model IDs dynamically returned by `GET /v1/models`. Do not guess model IDs or reuse them from memory.
* Select the endpoint from the model's `routes` list; prioritize the route marked `"preferred": true` when present.
* Do not assume a model supports a modality simply because its upstream family does. Always check `model_type` and `capabilities`.
* Listing models via `GET /v1/models` is free and allowed before the user approves any spend. Current prices are listed on [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models), not in these docs.

# AIsa Model Catalog: Model IDs, Routes, and Capabilities

> Find current AIsa model IDs, supported endpoints, and capabilities via GET /v1/models or the live catalog at aisa.one/models.

AIsa routes LLM, image, video, and embedding models through a single API key. Because models are frequently added and retired, this page explains how to query the catalog dynamically rather than maintaining a static list.

> **[GET /v1/models](#list-models-with-the-api)**
>
> Machine-readable list of model IDs, routes, and capability tags for applications and agents.

> **[aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models)**
>
> Browse, filter, and compare models, with current prices.

## List models with the API

Send your API key as a Bearer token. Listing models is free; requests without an API key return `402`.

```bash theme={null}
curl https://api.aisa.one/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY"
```

The response follows the standard OpenAI list format, extended with an `aisa` metadata object for each model:

```json theme={null}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "claude-fable-5-1",
      "object": "model",
      "created": 1788315984,
      "owned_by": "Anthropic",
      "aisa": {
        "display_name": "claude-fable-5-1",
        "model_type": "text",
        "capabilities": ["chat", "long-context", "reasoning", "tools"],
        "preferred_route": "anthropic",
        "routes": [
          { "key": "openai", "path": "/v1/chat/completions", "method": "POST" },
          { "key": "anthropic", "path": "/v1/messages", "method": "POST", "preferred": true }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `id` | The exact string to pass as `model`. |
| `owned_by` | Upstream provider, such as `OpenAI`, `Anthropic`, or `Alibaba`. |
| `aisa.model_type` | `text`, `image`, `video`, or `embedding`. |
| `aisa.capabilities` | Capability tags, such as `chat`, `tools`, `reasoning`, `vision`, `image`, `videos`, or `embeddings`. |
| `aisa.routes` | Every AIsa endpoint serving this model, specified as `method` + `path`. |
| `aisa.preferred_route` | Present on some models. The `key` of the recommended route (which also has `"preferred": true`). |

Filter the list with `jq`:

```bash theme={null}
# Models served by the Anthropic-compatible /v1/messages endpoint
curl -s https://api.aisa.one/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.data[] | select(any(.aisa.routes[]; .path == "/v1/messages")) | .id'

# Image models
curl -s https://api.aisa.one/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.data[] | select(.aisa.model_type == "image") | .id'
```

## Endpoints by model type

| Model type | Endpoints | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| Text | `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `POST /v1/messages`, `POST /v1/responses` | Most text models serve both OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible routes. Check `routes` before switching protocols. |
| Image | `POST /v1/images/generations`, `POST /v1/images/edits` | Not every image model supports edits. |
| Video | `POST /v1/video/generations`, then `GET /v1/video/generations/{task_id}` | Asynchronous: submit a job, then poll for the result. |
| Embedding | `POST /v1/embeddings` | |

Calling a model on an unsupported route returns `400` with `error.code` set to `model_route_not_supported`; `error.supported_routes` lists the routes that work. Request and response schemas for each endpoint are documented in the [API Reference](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/chat/post_chat-completions.md).

Point any OpenAI-compatible SDK at `https://api.aisa.one/v1` and pass a model `id` from the catalog:

```python theme={null}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key="YOUR_AISA_API_KEY", base_url="https://api.aisa.one/v1")

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen3.7-max",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Compare these model options for a coding agent."}],

print(response.choices[0].message.content)

# OpenAI-Compatible Image Generations

> Generate images with Seedream, Wan, gpt-image-2, and GPT Image 2.5 via the standard POST /v1/images/generations endpoint. OpenAI-compatible request shape; Seedream routes require a minimum image size of 3,686,400 pixels (e.g., 1920×1920).

The standard OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/images/generations` endpoint. As of September 30, 2026 it serves `seedream-5-0-260128`, `wan2.7-image`, `wan2.7-image-pro`, `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`. No image model is served on `POST /v1/chat/completions` — image generation goes through this endpoint (and `POST /v1/images/edits` where noted).

## Routing at a glance

| Model | Endpoint |
| - | - |
| `seedream-5-0-260128` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)* |
| `wan2.7-image` / `wan2.7-image-pro` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `gpt-image-2` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `gpt-image-2.5-flare` / `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| Gemini-compatible models | [`POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/chat/post_models-model-generatecontent) |

## Supported models

| Model | Billed by | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `seedream-5-0-260128` | Per request | Min image size **3,686,400 pixels** (e.g., 1920×1920) |
| `wan2.7-image` | Per request | Also accepts `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `wan2.7-image-pro` | Per request | Higher-quality Wan route |
| `gpt-image-2` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache write | See [AI Model Pricing](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/pricing.md#models) |
| `gpt-image-2.5-flare` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read | GPT Image 2.5 route |
| `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read | GPT Image 2.5 route |

Current prices are on [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models).

## Size constraint ⚠️ (Seedream routes)

Seedream's upstream enforces a minimum of **3,686,400 pixels**. Requests below that are rejected with:

```
400 InvalidParameter: image size must be at least 3686400 pixels
```

| Size | Pixels | Accepted? |
| - | - | - |
| `1024x1024` | 1,048,576 | ❌ |
| `1536x1536` | 2,359,296 | ❌ |
| `1920x1920` | 3,686,400 | ✅ (exact threshold) |
| `2048x2048` | 4,194,304 | ✅ |
| `2304x1600` | 3,686,400 | ✅ |
| `2560x1920` | 4,915,200 | ✅ |

Any aspect ratio works as long as `width × height ≥ 3,686,400`.

## Request

```bash curl theme={null}
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.aisa.one/v1/images/generations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "seedream-5-0-260128",
    "prompt": "A cute red panda, ultra-detailed, cinematic lighting",
    "n": 1,
    "size": "2048x2048"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.aisa.one/v1", api_key="sk-aisa-...")

resp = client.images.generate(
    model="seedream-5-0-260128",
    prompt="A cute red panda, ultra-detailed, cinematic lighting",
    n=1,
    size="2048x2048",
)

for item in resp.data:
    print(item.url)
```

```typescript TypeScript theme={null}
import OpenAI from "openai";

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://api.aisa.one/v1",
  apiKey: process.env.AISA_API_KEY,
});

const resp = await client.images.generate({
  model: "seedream-5-0-260128",
  prompt: "A cute red panda, ultra-detailed, cinematic lighting",
  n: 1,
  size: "2048x2048",
});

for (const item of resp.data) {
  console.log(item.url);
}
```

### Request fields

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| - | - | - | - |
| `model` | string | yes | One of `seedream-5-0-260128`, `wan2.7-image`, `wan2.7-image-pro`, `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` |
| `prompt` | string | yes | Text description of the image to generate |
| `n` | integer | no | Number of images. A per-request model charges one request price whatever `n` is; a token-priced model charges the tokens it reports |
| `size` | string | no | `WIDTHxHEIGHT`. Seedream routes must satisfy `width × height ≥ 3,686,400`; `wan2.7-image` and `gpt-image-2` accept smaller sizes (`1024x1024` verified working) |

## Response

```json theme={null}
{
  "model": "seedream-5-0-260128",
  "created": 1776495432,
  "data": [
    {
      "url": "https://cdn.aisa.one/images/seedream/...",
      "size": "2048x2048"
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "generated_images": 1,
    "output_tokens": 16384,
    "total_tokens": 16384
  }
}
```

**AIsa's response adds a few extensions** over the vanilla OpenAI schema:

* `model` echoed at the root
* `data[].size` — actual dimensions of each returned image
* `usage` — as the model reports it, for example `generated_images`, `output_tokens` and `total_tokens`. Token-priced models are charged from the token counts; per-request models are charged once per request

> [!WARNING]
>
> URLs in `data[].url` are **short-lived**. Download and persist the image to your own storage before it expires.

## Common 4xx causes

* `400 InvalidParameter — image size must be at least 3686400 pixels` — `size` was too small. Use `1920x1920` or larger.
* `400 model_route_not_supported` — the model doesn't serve this endpoint (e.g., a text model like `gpt-4.1-mini`). The error body's `supported_routes` lists the routes it does serve.
* `404 model not found` — the model ID doesn't exist on the gateway (e.g., the retired `seedream-4-5-251128`). Check the [model catalog](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/models.md).
* `400 invalid_request` — malformed `size` string (e.g., `1024` instead of `1024x1024`).

See [Error Codes](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/errors.md) and [Rate Limits](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/rate-limits.md) for more.

# OpenAI-Compatible Image Generations

> Generate images with Seedream, Wan, gpt-image-2, and GPT Image 2.5 via the standard POST /v1/images/generations endpoint. OpenAI-compatible request shape; Seedream routes require a minimum image size of 3,686,400 pixels (e.g., 1920×1920).

The standard OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/images/generations` endpoint. As of September 30, 2026 it serves `seedream-5-0-260128`, `wan2.7-image`, `wan2.7-image-pro`, `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, and `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`. No image model is served on `POST /v1/chat/completions` — image generation goes through this endpoint (and `POST /v1/images/edits` where noted).

## Routing at a glance

| Model | Endpoint |
| - | - |
| `seedream-5-0-260128` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)* |
| `wan2.7-image` / `wan2.7-image-pro` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `gpt-image-2` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `gpt-image-2.5-flare` / `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | **`POST /v1/images/generations`** *(this page)*, `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| Gemini-compatible models | [`POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent`](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/chat/post_models-model-generatecontent) |

## Supported models

| Model | Billed by | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `seedream-5-0-260128` | Per request | Min image size **3,686,400 pixels** (e.g., 1920×1920) |
| `wan2.7-image` | Per request | Also accepts `POST /v1/images/edits` |
| `wan2.7-image-pro` | Per request | Higher-quality Wan route |
| `gpt-image-2` | Per request or per image; token pricing also applies on some routes | See [AI Model Pricing](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/pricing.md#models) |
| `gpt-image-2.5-flare` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read | GPT Image 2.5 route |
| `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` | Per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read | GPT Image 2.5 route |

Current prices are on [aisa.one/models](https://aisa.one/models).

## Size constraint ⚠️ (Seedream routes)

Seedream's upstream enforces a minimum of **3,686,400 pixels**. Requests below that are rejected with:

```
400 InvalidParameter: image size must be at least 3686400 pixels
```

| Size | Pixels | Accepted? |
| - | - | - |
| `1024x1024` | 1,048,576 | ❌ |
| `1536x1536` | 2,359,296 | ❌ |
| `1920x1920` | 3,686,400 | ✅ (exact threshold) |
| `2048x2048` | 4,194,304 | ✅ |
| `2304x1600` | 3,686,400 | ✅ |
| `2560x1920` | 4,915,200 | ✅ |

Any aspect ratio works as long as `width × height ≥ 3,686,400`.

## Request

```bash curl theme={null}
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.aisa.one/v1/images/generations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AISA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "seedream-5-0-260128",
    "prompt": "A cute red panda, ultra-detailed, cinematic lighting",
    "n": 1,
    "size": "2048x2048"
  }'
```

```python Python theme={null}
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="https://api.aisa.one/v1", api_key="sk-aisa-...")

resp = client.images.generate(
    model="seedream-5-0-260128",
    prompt="A cute red panda, ultra-detailed, cinematic lighting",
    n=1,
    size="2048x2048",
)

for item in resp.data:
    print(item.url)
```

  n: 1,

});

for (const item of resp.data) {
  console.log(item.url);
}
```

### Request fields

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| - | - | - | - |
| `model` | string | yes | One of `seedream-5-0-260128`, `wan2.7-image`, `wan2.7-image-pro`, `gpt-image-2`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` |
| `prompt` | string | yes | Text description of the image to generate |
| `n` | integer | no | Number of images. Each is billed separately at the model's per-request rate |
| `size` | string | no | `WIDTHxHEIGHT`. Seedream routes must satisfy `width × height ≥ 3,686,400`; `wan2.7-image` and `gpt-image-2` accept smaller sizes (`1024x1024` verified working) |

## Response

```json theme={null}
{
  "model": "seedream-5-0-260128",
  "created": 1776495432,
  "data": [
    {
      "url": "https://cdn.aisa.one/images/seedream/...",
      "size": "2048x2048"
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "generated_images": 1,
    "output_tokens": 16384,
    "total_tokens": 16384
  }
}
```

**AIsa's response adds a few extensions** over the vanilla OpenAI schema:

* `model` echoed at the root
* `data[].size` — actual dimensions of each returned image
* `usage` — includes `generated_images` (drives billing), plus `output_tokens` / `total_tokens` for token accounting

> [!WARNING]
>
> URLs in `data[].url` are **short-lived**. Download and persist the image to your own storage before it expires.

## Common 4xx causes

* `400 InvalidParameter — image size must be at least 3686400 pixels` — `size` was too small. Use `1920x1920` or larger.
* `400 model_route_not_supported` — the model doesn't serve this endpoint (e.g., a text model like `gpt-4.1-mini`). The error body's `supported_routes` lists the routes it does serve.
* `404 model not found` — the model ID doesn't exist on the gateway (e.g., the retired `seedream-4-5-251128`). Check the [model catalog](https://aisa.one/docs/guides/models.md).
* `400 invalid_request` — malformed `size` string (e.g., `1024` instead of `1024x1024`).

See [Error Codes](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/errors.md) and [Rate Limits](https://aisa.one/docs/api-reference/rate-limits.md) for more.
